Every source line citation re-verified against the pinned checkouts before filing. All `inspire` (Py/C++→Go, no bytes vendored).
- [Windows handles, consoles, and spawn storms: which ceilings are real (2026-07-08)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-windows-handles-terminal-limits-2026-07-08.md) — deep research + a live probe of the agent host, answering "why is the Windows handles/terminal thing such an issue, and why isn't it tunable?" Three unrelated failures were conflated under one name. **Kernel handles are not the ceiling**: 16,711,680 per *process*, hard-coded with no registry knob, against 243,735 system-wide on this box — the `find` incident was a leak whose real risk is paged-pool exhaustion (`ERROR_NO_SYSTEM_RESOURCES` 1450), not a count cap. The **pwsh `0xE9` FailFast (#2170) is a ConPTY-chain fragility bug, not a limit** — there is no cap on consoles/pseudoconsoles and no tunable; pwsh treats `GetConsoleScreenBufferInfo` as infallible and calls `Environment.FailFast()` when the console peer dies. The **low-usage stall (#3153) is `CreateProcess` cost** (>20× Linux) plus soft-fault contention on the PFN/working-set locks, invisible to CPU/RAM/disk meters by construction. The knobs everyone reaches for — `GDIProcessHandleQuota`, `USERProcessHandleQuota`, `SharedSection` — *are* tunable and *are* red herrings (headless processes never touching user32 don't consume them); `MaxUserPort` is deprecated. Witnessed: **`WindowsTerminal` is the top handle *and* thread holder on this host (17,582 / 902)** — the same process that froze dispatch on 2026-07-01 — so the "terminal handles thing" is app-level accretion in the emulator, not an OS refusal. Names two gaps in our own tooling (`host_stall_mitigations.ps1` uses only `-ExclusionProcess`, which per MS Learn does *not* stop Defender scanning the executable image on each spawn; `internal/stallscan` carries no handle axis) and names **Job Objects** (`ActiveProcessLimit` + `KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`) as the unused kernel control surface for orphans and spawn admission. Ranked tune-now vs redesign vs do-not-touch.

- [The claim-space IS the disaggregation primitive — one partition algebra, two planes (2026-07-08)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-CLAIM-SPACE-IS-THE-DISAGGREGATION-PRIMITIVE-2026-07-08.md) — the through-line that fak's control-plane claim-space (`dos arbitrate` / `laneadmit` / `regionadmit` / `dispatchorder.Plan`, claiming file trees by tree-disjointness) and its compute-plane disaggregation (`NativePDCluster` P/D, `ExpertParallelPlan`, `TPPlan`, `kvmmu` tiers, `DistComm`, claiming compute regions by data-disjointness) are **one partition algebra at two granularities**: `dispatchorder.Candidate{Lane,Tree,Mode}` read fresh is a resource request, and disaggregation is that primitive at a finer grain — scale-free from phone/IoT (one-at-a-time) to a hyperscaler mesh (100s–1000s of claimable units). The gap is that the two planes don't share an admission kernel; the fusion advantage (`polymodel` co-residency split at the tool-call-as-syscall seam) is the split point. Tagged `[SHIPPED]`/`[SEAM-ONLY]`/`[GAP]`, asserts no benchmark number. Tracked as **epic #3259** (children #3268–#3271).

- [Concept: anti-starvation dispatch aging — no ready unit waits forever (2026-07-11)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-DISPATCH-AGING-2026-07-11.md) — the missing feedback term in the issue→worker dispatch order: today `dispatchtick.OrderLaneCandidates` and `dispatchorder.Plan` rank ready work by base priority **absolutely** (age only breaks ties), so a light unit out-weighed by a steady drip of fresher high-priority arrivals is never picked — textbook priority starvation, which `dispatch-conservation` can only see *after the fact* as re-storm churn. `internal/dispatchaging` folds each unit's wait time into an **effective weight** (`base + aging_boost`, monotonic ⇒ eventually overtakes any fixed heavier tier) plus a **hard starvation deadline** (waited ≥ 6h ⇒ force-served this tick, bounding worst-case wait independent of the boost math); `Standing` is the closed `fresh|aging|starved` fairness verdict. **Shipped**: the pure fold + property tests (additive — zero `Params` reproduces the pre-aging order), and `fak dispatch-aging` as a read-only JSON diagnostic with a `--fail-on-starved` CI gate. **Gap**: the live picker doesn't yet consume the term (computed & reported, not enforced) — the first of five parked follow-ons, alongside a `dos.toml [dispatch.aging]` config, real `ReadySince` provenance, starvation observability, and cooldown-eligibility interaction.
- [Durable handling of guard false positives: match on structure, not mention (2026-07-02)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-GUARD-FALSE-POSITIVE-DURABILITY-2026-07-02.md) — the reversibility classifier ([#2376](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2376)) escalates commands that merely MENTION a trigger word (`git commit -m "...push"`, `grep "git push"`, `echo "rm -rf"`) and is simultaneously evadable by wrapping the same command in a script — one antipattern, matching on substring not call structure, wrong in both directions at once. Durable design in three layers: the structural-match doctrine (classify on the executed segment head / resolved target / egress host, never on payload mention; SQL and `dd` scans are the named payload-inspection whitelist), a growing false/true-positive corpus with a measured false-positive rate folded as a `guard-accuracy` scorecard, and a logged escape hatch (the shipped `29b98f26` in-band confirm recipe + a proposed `fak guard false-positive` ledger) so a routed-around escalation always leaves a trace. Names the second-order instance (the coarse `internal/adjudicator/**` hard-self glob firing on a non-self-grading preview classifier).

- [Multi-node concurrent development groundwork (2026-07-02)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/MULTINODE-DEV-GROUNDWORK-2026-07-02.md) — design note for epic [#2254](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2254) (children #2297/#2299/#2300/#2302/#2304): how lease state, presence, and intent TRAVEL between hardware nodes, as three planes speaking one vocabulary — plane 0 git-carried `refs/fak/locks/*` converged by the new `fak leaseref sync` (shipped: push-then-fetch order load-bearing, fail-fast on push, no prune by design, deletions converge via TTL+reap), plane 1 the gateway dev-server (read endpoints, then single-arbiter fenced acquire — the only honest closure of the cross-machine atomicity gap), plane 2 GH-comment announce (evidence, never a lock). Plus the node-identity convention (`<node-id>/<session-id>`) and the target per-tick protocol (sync → reap → arbitrate → fenced acquire → fence-before-write → renew → publish).
- [The Slack control plane: one durable wire out, one authorized door in (2026-07-02)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SLACK-CONTROL-FOUNDATION-2026-07-02.md) — design note + SOTA survey for epic [#2259](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2259) (children #2261–#2268): what HEAD has (14 fire-and-forget outbound surfaces over two parallel clients; chatrelay-only inbound, deliberately not control), the dgx-bridge/fakrpc invariants recast as design rules (detach, out-of-band results, nonce-spool idempotency, single-writer drain, leak fence, structured capacity refusals), the verified 2025 Slack rate-limit terms (internal customer-built apps exempt — polling legal, strictly inferior to Socket Mode), outbound durability facts (no server-side idempotency exists; outbox + metadata-key + update-coalescing is the honest at-least-once contract), the HITL survey (Claude-in-Slack/Devin/Copilot/Codex/HumanLayer/LangGraph), the Go websocket landscape (`coder/websocket` consensus; hand-rolled Socket Mode ≈300 lines), and the chatops security fence: channel text is never instructions — closed verbs or refusal.
- [The tool process table: mastering long-running tool use (2026-07-02)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-TOOL-PROCESS-TABLE-2026-07-02.md) — the tool-call-granularity row the no-babysitting doctrine leaves open: fak disposes a call at admission and its payload at re-entry, but a background shell / monitor / polled job crosses the floor as uncorrelated events with no deadline, stall, orphan, or post-kill control. Ships the decision spine (`internal/toolproc` pure fold + `fak toolproc ps|sample`; closed verdicts TOOL_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED→kill, TOOL_HEARTBEAT_STALLED→probe, TOOL_ORPHANED→reap, TOOL_RESULT_AFTER_KILL→quarantine_result at out-of-tree reason codes 1040–1043) and maps the six enforcement seams (gateway supervisor, result-admission rung, MCP progress/cancel, harness hooks, policy runtime envelope, procguard binding) as labeled next steps.
- [Safe concurrency headroom on the agent host (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SAFE-CONCURRENCY-HEADROOM-2026-07-01.md) — witnessed capacity audit of the one-box fleet: `host_cap`=16 (cores-bound) with 178 GB RAM free while the dispatcher sits at **0 live workers** because one PROTECTED foreign process (the operator's own terminal, 2,767 threads) trips `host_check()`'s any-flag fold into a fleet-wide REFUSE_HOST — a liveness bug, not a safety win. Ranks the safe raise-concurrency levers: the REFUSE_HOST carve-out (advisory for protected non-fleet flags), seats as the true multiplier (each seat safe by construction at one worker per account), static caps raised to the design intent so the adaptive gates govern, an elevated reaper for Session-0 zombie threads, measured per-worker charge constants, and the scaffolding (guard front door, ~3-spawn waves, lane leases, witnessed closes) that must scale with the count. Ceiling estimate: ~4–5 tonight, ~7 after 2026-07-04, hardware green to 16.
- [fak guard's share of cache value on real sessions — proven (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/FAK-GUARD-CACHE-VALUE-SHARE-2026-07-01.md) — the epic [#1844](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1844) headline split, measured from the durable ledgers: on 11 real `fak guard -- claude` sessions the provider prompt cache accounts for 153.1M token-equiv and fak's own mechanisms for **0 (0.0000%)** — the compaction-row absence is a witness, not a gap, because the same guard-exit writer emits both mechanisms; folding the `fak run` kernel sessions in, fak's witnessed slice is 3,441 tokens (**0.0022%**). `fak cachevalue report` now prints the pre-divided `fak_share` per period (refused with `-` when a period total is not positive) and carries `fak_share_pct` in the JSON, with scope fences (placement is identity on Claude Code, managed-cache TTL gated off, recorded rows only) and the #1844 levers that would move the number.
- [One binary, eleven orders of magnitude: the dynamic-range contract (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/DYNAMIC-RANGE-ONE-BINARY-2026-07-01.md) — doctrine note + epic [#2218](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2218) (children #2219–#2224) for fak's temporal dynamic range: one Go binary adjudicates a tool call in ~0.4–2.4 µs (`Decide` 362 ns/op) and orients a days-long `superloop walk tend` intent — the band ladder B0→B7 with witnessed anchors, the five one-binary wins (one closed refusal vocabulary across clocks, one admission structure, transport collapse as a repeatable move, one witness discipline, one budget-envelope shape), the risk register each win drags in (monoculture blast radius; version skew across running copies — witnessed: `fak version` prints "no VCS stamp"; fail-open vDSO budget coverage; backpressure that flows down but not up; cross-band causality per the SWE-bench empty-patch case; runtime-tail coupling), six laws, and the gap→ticket table (G1 vDSO budget row #2219, G2 provenance/skew witness #2220, G3 gate-pressure cap term #2221, G4 budget cascade #2222, G5 full-span trace + loaded p99 #2223, drive rung #2224). Keeps the gate-ladder fence: different clocks never multiply into one end-to-end number.
- [Meaningful control, one sidecar, automatic context: the three-plane split (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-CONTROL-SIDECAR-AUTOCTX-2026-07-01.md) — disambiguation + strategy for the operator's three-theme goal: one litmus test (*a knob belongs to the user iff it encodes intent the system cannot infer*) splits every knob into an INTENT plane the user meaningfully controls (epic [#2208](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2208), children #2210–#2212: knob census, `fak session pin`, envelope wall/spend/throughput routes), a LEGIBILITY plane — the sidecar/rollup view where the same session/account/lane/posture facts and shared items render identically across agents, surfaces, and hosts (epic [#2209](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2209), children #2213–#2216: cross-agent census, session-descriptor join schema, parity-witnessed pane, shared items live) — and the HOUSEKEEPING plane that stays zero-knob automatic under the existing #2198/#1844 programs. Two opposing ratchets (R1 #2199 down on housekeeping knobs; A1 #2210 down on route-less intent levers) keep the boundary honest; the operator's own example lands as INTENT = `fak session branch` (#1200) vs HOUSEKEEPING = routine carryover (#2198 R5/R7).
- [No babysitting: nobody watches a healthy fleet (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-NO-BABYSITTING-2026-07-01.md) — the attention doctrine that makes unattended operation a falsifiable product property, and the umbrella over the automatic-context (#2198), perpetual-sessions (#1860), and loop-kernel notes: babysitting is *polling*, and the kernel's job is to convert every poll into a rare, cheap, evidence-carrying interrupt. Decomposes supervision labor into seven watches (liveness, truth, safety, collision, budget, unblock, quality/goal-fit), argues which ones the improving model/harness slope retires vs **intensifies** (the trust asymmetry is structural; fan-out outruns constant attention; blast radius grows with delegated privilege; concurrency grows races; crashes are infra-shaped — the 2026-07-01 bottleneck map's recovery-layer CRITICAL is the datapoint), states seven laws (poll→interrupt; green means witnessed, not quiet; every interrupt is a typed packet; silence is bounded; autonomy is earned mechanically; recovery is the default path; the residual is human on purpose), defines the babysitting counter (touches per witnessed unit, silent hours, session MTTR, escalation handling time), and names rungs R1–R6 (counter → escalation packet → waiting-on-human queue → recovery drain witness → autonomy ratchet → unattended soak witness). Filed 2026-07-02 as epic [#2269](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2269) with labeled children #2270–#2277.
- [A surfaced choice is a triage, not a page (2026-07-07)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-CHOICE-IS-A-TRIAGE-2026-07-07.md) — the decision-side dual of the no-babysitting doctrine (#2269): before bounding how a human page behaves, ask whether the page was genuine at all. Almost every choice a fleet surfaces is fake — fold it honestly and it lands in one of four places: `TAKE_OBVIOUS` (one sane move an agent just takes), `FRESH_CONTEXT` (knowable but not obvious → a fresh context window at the top model tier), `FILE_TICKET` (real work too big for one context → a GH ticket), or `HUMAN_RESIDUAL` (a genuine policy/auth/release/priority/trust call — the only case that waits). The load-bearing inversion: the default is `FRESH_CONTEXT`, never `HUMAN_RESIDUAL`; a human decision must be *earned* by a signal naming authority a person holds, so the residual shrinks toward zero. Shipped: `internal/choicetriage` (tier-1, pure, closed `Disposition` vocab + deterministic `Triage`) and its first consumer `internal/operatorbrief` (every `Choice` now carries `Disposition`/`Resolve`/`NeedsHuman`; a missing-report page with a runnable fix becomes `TAKE_OBVIOUS`, a release go/no-go stays `HUMAN_RESIDUAL`). Filed as epic [#3136](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3136) with the worktype-unification rung [#3137](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3137).

- [Automatic context: nobody manages the window (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-AUTOMATIC-CONTEXT-2026-07-01.md) — concept note + epic [#2198](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/2198) (children #2199–#2206): the zero-knob doctrine that binds the managed-context (#1570), relay (#1860), cache-default (#1490), prompt-MMU (#751/#1258), and ctxplan (#844) programs to one falsifiable product property: *nobody — human or agent — manages the context window*. States the virtual-memory thesis (every manual `/compact`, hand-written handoff baton, "don't read that file," breakpoint, or TTL choice is a hand-written overlay), the two-sides-of-one-coin unification (residency in the window and warmth in the caches are projections of one address space, priced by **one ledger**, decided together), seven laws (one manager per wire; the window is a view; removal is placement; one coin; zero knobs on the default path; abstain honestly; every surface declares its context plan), a HEAD-verified wiring map (live pipeline vs dormant `syspromptmmu`/`memview`/`ctxresidency` vs gated-off vCache loop), the manual-overlay inventory (H1–H5 human, A1–A4 agent, plus server-side), a per-surface infusion table, and rungs R1–R8 (manual-overlay counter → one-ledger join → placement dual-write → context-plan-required gate → auto-envelope → retire the big-file warning → relay-by-default → the witnessing readout). Honest fences: bulk-closed managed-context children are design-shipped until #1918 witnesses the contract; WITNESSED never blended with OBSERVED.

- [Native-harness progress tracking (#1315) (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/native-harness-progress-tracking-1315.md) — the roll-up for [epic #1315](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1315), *fak owns the native agent loop end-to-end — the dispatch-edge program*. On the proxy path the external harness (Claude Code/codex) owns the turn loop and *consumes* tool calls outside fak; the native harness is fak *owning* dispatch (its own loop drives the turns, the kernel is the only tool path), the precondition for every "impossible on proxy" capability (vDSO tool-result materialization, before-consumption write barrier, speculative serve). Produced from an **8-surface, 90-claim survey** whose every SHIPPED/PARTIAL claim was re-checked by an adversarial pass against git + request-path reachability — **27 downgrades** on the one question that matters: *is there a live, non-test caller on the request path?* The honest one-liner: **the engine is owned, the loop is not (yet).** SHIPPED + live on the serve path: the native `/v1/messages` front door, in-kernel generation (`--gguf`), in-kernel tool-call render+lift+adjudication, fail-closed on malformed calls, vDSO read-serve, per-request session admission, the context planner, KV planned-elision, inbound quarantine, the `fak guard` proxy gate, the syscall boundary + A/B comparator. PARTIAL (built + tested, **zero live caller**): `RunArm` itself (only the `fak agent` benchmark + bench/ablate callers; the served path is single-shot `s.planner.Complete`), `WithSessionTable`/`gateTurn`, `drainSteer`, `WithRouteManifest`, `ApplyPace`, `WaitResume` warm-KV splice, in-loop streaming, the AgentDojo steward sweep, the multi-session scheduler, the intent conduit (#805), the loop-lifecycle ledger. NOT_YET (named gaps, keystones first): the **suspend-and-resume turn primitive** (`gateTurn` *terminates*, it does not suspend — the one net-new mechanism the canonical note names) and the **before-consumption write barrier** (SEAM-4 `abi/speculate.go` is committed `d859ec21` but `Speculator.Predict` has zero production callers), plus the consistency-level field on `ToolCall`, the native TUI/REPL (`fak chat`), and the system-prompt-MMU spine's first live caller. 8 ordered children #1316–#1323 (keystones #1316 a live `RunArm` caller, #1318 the suspend/resume primitive). Forward framing in [the vToolcall fork note](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/VTOOLCALL-FORK-AND-BESTEFFORT-2026-06-25.md); close children per [the epic close-out method](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/EPIC-CLOSEOUT-METHOD-2026-06-29.md) (a CLOSED box is a self-report, not a witness).
- [Epic close-out method — properly closing (or retiring) an epic (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/EPIC-CLOSEOUT-METHOD-2026-06-29.md) — the backlog is epic-heavy (57/171 open are epics); this is the repeatable method for closing one **honestly**. Guards the two failure modes — *false-close* (a child's `CLOSED` state / `- [x]` box is a self-report, not a witness; the syspromptmmu #1258 children were docs-closed while the code stayed UNBUILT) and *stale-open* (shipped epics that nobody re-checked). Three routes: **A COMPLETED** — every child closed AND the deliverable witnessed in the tracked tree (artifact on disk + claimed SHAs real + `dos commit-audit` OK/diff-witnessed + residual carved), closed with the #1147 house-style evidence comment (worked example: **#1116** closed 2026-06-29); **B NOT_PLANNED** — superseded/deduped, point to the survivor and fold framing there (example #1226→#1217; candidate clusters: serving #50/#637/#931, agent-OS #748/#749/#750/#1178/#1193); **C STANDING** — a "keep-the-scorecard-alive" perpetual loop (#710/#801/#1050/#1278) is retired from the deliverable count (split finite children out, drive the recurring part from a `/loop`, mark standing), never closed as done. Includes the read-only bulk close-state audit recipe and the anti-gaming laws.
- [The native-code doctrine (#1124) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/NATIVE-CODE-DOCTRINE-1124-2026-06-28.md) — fak's written rule for dropping below portable Go: Go-assembly (`.s`) is welcome on the model/compute path and is **not** cgo; `cgo`/`import "C"` is justified only for GPU device code behind an opt-in build tag; neither is ever allowed on the request/adjudication path. Plus the verified backlog of hot scalar kernels worth vectorizing (C1–C6) and the four places native code must never go.
- [Committing shared-clone WIP is an integration pass, not a freeze (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SHARED-CLONE-INTEGRATION-PASS-2026-06-29.md) — runbook for an agent told to commit/clean up work in progress on the shared fak clone: land complete, self-contained, building units by explicit path; park the rest; gate the push with an archive-HEAD build — instead of mislabeling collective fleet WIP as untouchable peer work.
- [fak issue-backlog dispatch loop — handoff (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/DISPATCH-LOOP-HANDOFF-2026-06-29.md) — handoff from a session that shipped 26 issues via headless lane-disjoint workers: the paste-ready goal prompt, that session's laws, and a live backlog probe (the adversarial red-team pass was cut by a session limit, so the tooling sketches are proposals, not vetted specs).
- [GLM-5.2 multi-GPU: expert-parallel sharding + the resident-fit benchmark (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/GLM52-EXPERT-PARALLEL-MULTIGPU-2026-06-29.md) — the **expert-parallel (EP) MoE FFN decomposition** for GLM-5.2 is now host-proven on trunk (`internal/model/expert_parallel.go`, `f713391c`): partition the experts across ranks (`ExpertParallelPlan`, a named `TPPlan` over `[0,NumExperts)`), each rank computes only the picks it owns, one `AllReduceSum` of the per-rank `[H]` delta — the cheap MoE-native multi-GPU decomposition `forwardTPSupported()` fails closed on, and the one the overnight cpu-offload data points to (move the expert GEMM off the host onto idle GPUs). The gate triad runs with **no multi-GPU hardware** (`LocalCollective`): `EP(ranks=1)`==routed monolith **max\|Δ\|=0**, collective==rank-order ref **max\|Δ\|=0** (ranks 1/2/4/8), `EP(ranks=N)` cosine 1.0 (~3.7e-9 reassociation drift), + load-imbalance + fail-closed + a GLM shared-expert wrapper on a real `glm_moe_dsa` fixture. Makes the first **benchmark** answerable: the GPU server's **8×80GB = 640 GiB** VRAM (WITNESSED) fits GLM-5.2 UD-Q4_K_M (**433.82 GiB**, ~54 GiB/GPU even shard + replicated dense + KV ≈ 55–60 GiB/GPU < 80, ~20 GiB headroom, COMPUTED) — so **resident EP is feasible by capacity**, the lever past the measured 0.2324 tok/s cpu-offload wall (vs 0.89 tok/s llama.cpp CPU). Honest scope: the primitive is landed but **not yet** wired into the live forward, and a live resident-EP tok/s witness is gated on three rungs — a real cross-DEVICE NCCL/RCCL collective (CUDA still `cudaSetDevice(0)`, `Caps.Collective=false`), EP live-wiring, and a multi-GPU binary on the box (Go absent). The cpu-offload wall stands as the baseline until then.
- [Blackwell-class hardware readiness map (GB200/GB300 NVL72) (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/BLACKWELL-NVL72-READINESS-MAP-2026-06-29.md) — a grounded plan for running fak better on the latest NVIDIA datacenter hardware. Thesis: fak's scale-out architecture is already **NVL72-shaped** — a coherent KV-**pool** plane (`internal/cachemeta/pool.go` `FabricShareable()`), a hardware-aware residency **ladder** (`hardware.go`, HBM→DRAM→NUMA-far→CXL→Disk), a device-**mesh** collective seam (`compute.go` `CollectiveBackend`), and a bit-exact middle-span **evict** that survives paging (`paged_evict.go`, `#33` GO) — but **every one is a stub today** (a cost model, a CPU-ref collective, `cudaSetDevice(0)`, no FP4 enum). A GB300 NVL72 (one coherent **20.7 TB** HBM3e NVLink domain across 72 GPUs + 36 Grace CPUs, **130 TB/s** in-domain NVLink, **NVFP4** at 0.5 B/param, ~900 GB/s Grace coherent memory) is the physical substrate those planes were written against. Maps each Blackwell lever onto the exact seam it lights up (file-anchored, with `[SHIPPED]`/`[SEAM-ONLY]`/`[GAP]` state), names the four contexts where fak's *specific* levers compound (fleet prefix reuse across a coherent domain; demote-not-evict against a 900 GB/s tier; KV disaggregation at 1.8 TB/s NVLink ~18–36× the planned TCP path; the frontier class in-reach as FP4 weights stop dominating HBM and KV governance becomes the scarce resource), resolves the **one load-bearing tension** (NVFP4 vs the bit-exact-evict moat → tier precision per *plane*: FP4 the weights + V + read-K, keep an f32 `Kraw` shadow for governably-evictable spans, the FP4 analogue of the `#1047` Q8-KV choice), and lays a **hardware-ungated-first** rung ladder (R0 FP4+BF16 `Dtype` + cpu-ref oracle, R1 FP4-KV tier the moat survives, R2 model the NVL72 in the cost planes, R3 KV→bytes serializer — all doable now; R5 NVFP4 device GEMM, R6 NCCL device collective, R7 NVLink/RDMA byte mover, R8 the governed mega-pool — Blackwell-gated). Strategic frame: the hardware doesn't make fak a *faster server* (vLLM/SGLang still win tok/s) — it makes fak's **governance** value mandatory, because a 20.7 TB coherent pool shared by a fleet *forces* the cross-tenant-reuse / provable-evict / placement / disaggregation questions only fak answers with attribution. Asserts **no** measured fak number on Blackwell; every figure is a published spec or a labelled MODELED cost-model projection (the `#44` parity-must-be-measured rule still binds).
- [Cache savings in one session: what fak did and didn't (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SESSION-CACHE-SAVINGS-ABLATION-2026-06-29.md) — ablates a `fak guard` session (`c6723f7c`, 122 turns) three ways — **no cache (~29.65M projected)**, **normal Anthropic cache (~4.15M, −86%)**, **fak guard (~4.15M, identical)** — to make the attribution honest: the `~25.5M input-token-equiv` headline is the **provider's** prompt cache, which fak **prices** (`cache_pricing.go`, OBSERVED not WITNESSED) but cannot move, because passthrough forwards `req.Raw` verbatim and the `cache_control` prefix stays byte-identical. fak's *own* contribution is a sliver of uncached tool-def tokens (tool-floor prune, ~0.1% of headline) and — the real lever — **1,104 bad tool calls stopped before a wasted round-trip** (1,101 repaired, 3 denied); compaction stayed idle. Also answers **"does that mean fak's features aren't on?"** with a HEAD-verified enablement audit — all six token-savers are default-on (`token_defaults.go`-locked) incl. `ctxview`/`elide` (flipped on 06-28/06-26; #927 closed the #555 passthrough gap), but the cache-breakpoint-near-the-end structure leaves fak only a small uncached tail to act on, by design (a referee), not a misconfig. Two-panel [ablation SVG](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/session-cache-ablation-2026-06-29.svg) + [enablement-status SVG](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/session-feature-enablement-2026-06-29.svg).
- [The cache-hit vanity metric: a self-fulfilling prophecy toward over-long sessions (2026-07-01)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CACHE-HIT-VANITY-METRIC-SELF-FULFILLING-2026-07-01.md) — the **incentive** layer under the [frozen-trajectory cache cliff](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/explainers/frozen-trajectory-cache-cliff.md): prompt-cache hit rate rises with trajectory length by construction (`(T-1)/(T+1)`), so reading it as an efficiency signal is a self-fulfilling prophecy toward over-long sessions — the *same* growing prefix that lifts the hit rate also raises the per-turn bill (19× at 200 turns) and drives context rot, and the "saved-token" headline is ~quadratic in length too. Names both sides (long is rewarded; cutting is punished by a visible hit dip yet repays its one cold prefix in a couple of turns), the counter-metrics to steer on instead (verified-progress-per-token via `dos_status`/`dos_commit_audit`, marginal-cost trend via `tools/ctxcost.py marginal`, flat context via the [relay](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-PERPETUAL-SESSIONS-2026-07-01.md)), and the many-agent corollary (short fresh agents + [pay-the-prefix-once](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/visuals/65-pay-the-prefix-once.svg), not the monolith a hit-rate maximizer would prefer). Runnable: `python tools/cache_curve.py inversion` (new `inversion` subcommand + `turn_cost`/`cum_cost`/`saved_headline`/`cut_break_even_turns`, math pinned by `CostInversion` tests).
- [Audit: recent fak logs — effectiveness + context fidelity (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/AUDIT-recent-fak-logs-effectiveness-fidelity-2026-06-28.md) — the **operational** companion to the [harness-cache-coherence design audit](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/HARNESS-CACHE-COHERENCE-AUDIT-2026-06-28.md), driven by the *recent* logs on the clone (`.fak/`). Answers the two questions directly. **(1) How effective?** From today's `recent-feature-dogfood` log: vCache `7.13×` telemetry readiness (one workload, OBSERVED), callavoid `2.46×` turn-amplification, cache-value `63%` realized reuse — but the load-bearing finding is the **honest ceiling**: `internal/cachevalueledger/ledger.go:111-119` hard-codes the only publishable framing as `~1.0× single-session (vs-naive 1/(1-reuse) excluded per #1066)`, and the `--floor 0.751` gate *correctly abstained* because `MinGateTurns=8` and only 5 turns were present. The dogfood's overall `ACTION` verdict comes from two **honest** failures, neither a context fault: a probe that refuses to call a *planned* 2× a *telemetry-witnessed* 2× (`recent_feature_dogfood.py:348-355` requires `active_source=="telemetry"`), and a transient assembler build error (`internal/model/quant_amd64_kquant.s` `CMPQ $0,AX` — green at HEAD when re-checked, so a stale-log artifact). **(2) How do we know it isn't butchering context?** Five tested invariants — verbatim-prefix byte-splice (`anthropic_compact.go`/`anthropic_elide.go`, a turn only counts `fired` if the protected prefix was byte-identical, else `prefix_mismatch`, `metrics.go:104`), bail-to-identity on any ambiguity with a closed reason vocabulary, bounded+marked+never-total elision loss (head+tail, last-4 working set untouched), the witness-gated quarantine moat (`recall.go:18-22`), and single-source WITNESSED/OBSERVED-separated attribution. Names the three **honest fidelity limits** rather than hiding them: KV prefix-elision is admittedly NOT bit-exact (`exact=false`, "a re-RoPE cannot un-see attended history", `kvmmu_elide_test.go:51-76`); the quarantine-survives-harness-summary hole is *detected* (`QuarantineAtRisk`) not fixed; and the `PreCompact` suppression **actuator is not yet wired** (`harness_coherence.go:283`, #1133 open) — fak today *measures* the harness butchering context but does not yet *prevent* it. Verdict: effectiveness REAL-but-fenced (passes net-true-value), fidelity STRONG-by-construction + HONEST-about-the-gaps. The mechanism even acted **live on the auditing session** (a `ctxview`-elided turn + a credential-shaped string paged out, both announced with a stub). Lists three checkable `not yet` follow-ons.
### The context-safety series (epic #1217)

- [Context-safety doctrine (#1218, C1 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-visuals-tracking-1217.md) — the C1 design note for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): states the **property** (context safety = value-preservation, the **dual** of the security floor — the security floor proves a *bad* call can't get *in*, this floor proves a *good* call's value doesn't silently get *lost* when fak sheds context, and shows it as a cross-checkable picture, not a number you must trust), grounded in why a single number can't carry it (the measured `ctxplan/signalnoise` cache-hit denominator artifact: 0.88→0.99 mechanically with length). Names the **context-event source of truth** — the hash-chained journal `internal/journal/journal.go:59-90` (`CAP_FAULT | CAP_EVICT | CAP_VERSION_BIND` rows, `Seq`/`PrevHash`/`Hash`/`Witness`, replayable via `Verify`/`VerifyRows`) plus the two secondary sources (`engine/capacity_adapter.go` `CacheEventRecorder`; `cachemeta/kvtransfer.go` `KVTransfer` ok/missed/fault). Decomposes "real retained value" into **four guarantees**, each bound to a real cited witness seam: **G1** bit-identity `max\|Δ\|=0` evict-correctness (`kvcache.go:44-105`; `paged_evict_test.go:84`, `longrope_test.go:179`), **G2** saved-vs-realized reuse-bit + correctness (WITNESSED `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_reused_tokens_total` `cachewitness.go:155` reconciled against `prefix_coherence.go:51`), **G3** S/N + Faults paired (`signalnoise.go` `Ratio()`/`FaultRatio()`/`Grade()` `starving`), **G4** cell-integrity (`recall.PageSyndrome` five-axis digest re-derivation). States the **self-checking-visual doctrine** (A paired-axis / B conservation roll-up / C provenance lane / D re-derivation, generalizing the `RestoreIndex(ix.Image()) == ix` rebuild-and-prove-equal pattern to the rendered visual) and the **honesty fences** (value-preservation kept distinct from the security floor AND the #1147 self-tax plane; WITNESSED/OBSERVED/MODELED never summed; an un-witnessed guarantee is a `not yet` not a result; design-only). Names the honest `not yet` gaps — the re-derivation witness (C9 #1227), the cell-integrity visual surface, the DOS refusal tokens (C13 #1231) — rather than rendering them green. Research/design only; sibling of the C2 failure-mode catalog [#1219](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1219).
- [Context-safety failure-mode catalog (#1219, C2 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-failure-mode-catalog-1217.md) — the C2 child of the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): every failure the value-preservation plane must surface, each mapped to its **witness** (the journal `Kind` / typed verdict / metric / test that catches it), the visual **primitive** that renders it, and the **cross-check** (paired-axis / conservation roll-up / provenance lane / re-derivation) that goes red on it. Six grounded rows — GDN evict panic (#1143, `RecurrentEvictUnsupportedError` + `fak_bgloop_up`-vs-decode-rate liveness light), evict-on-recurrent refused (the `refused` conservation segment), saved-but-never-reused (the WITNESSED `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_reused_tokens_total` gap chart, never blended with OBSERVED provider `cache_read`), S/N-up-but-faults-up (the `ctxplan/signalnoise` `Ratio()`+`FaultRatio()` `starving` grade), cell rot (#782 `recall.PageSyndrome`'s five-axis digest/quarantine/durability/witness/trust-epoch re-derivation), tier page-down missed (`cachemeta.KVTransfer` ok/missed/fault, ties #985) — each cited to a real `file:line`. Plus two failures with **no closing witness** kept as honest named gaps (rendered-visual-drift → C9/C10; harness-rewrite-defeats-the-shed → the `internal/compactcohere` follow-on), because the doctrine's rule is that a named gap is catalog content and only a *silent* gap is the invisible-destruction failure the epic exists to kill. Research/design only; sibling of the C1 doctrine note [#1218](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1218).
- [Context-safety saved-vs-realized gap (#1221, C4 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-saved-vs-realized-gap-1217.md) — the C4 value-decomposition spec (MVP slice) for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): the one value-gap that matters — **claimed-saved tokens at page-out time vs later-realized reuse** — built from two WITNESSED taps, **D1** (claimed-saved: journal `CAP_EVICT` row + `internal/engine/cacheevents.go:304-317` `CacheEventRecorder`) and **D2** (realized reuse: `internal/cachewitness` `KVPrefixWitness.ReuseRatio()` `cachewitness.go:155` over `fak_gateway_kv_prefix_reused_tokens_total` `metrics.go:1531`, fed by `cacheobs.Default.Snapshot()`). Specs the `SavedRealizedGap` datum (`Gap = ClaimedSaved - RealizedReused`, the error bar; a positive gap is an over-claim fak never realized), the cross-checks it carries (A paired-axis saved-with-realized + D re-derive both from tamper-evident sources, the C9 checker), and the load-bearing **provenance fence**: the gap is **never blended with the OBSERVED provider `cache_read`** — grounded in the measured cache-hit denominator artifact (`cache_read` climbs to ~1.0 mechanically with length, so a gap built on it would close to zero precisely when the window is most bloated). Binds guarantee G2 of the C1 doctrine (#1218); renders failure F3 of the C2 catalog (#1219); reconciled against the C14 coherence witness (#1232); re-derived by C9 (#1227). Research/design only.
- [Context-safety visual-primitive schemas (#1223, C6 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-visual-primitive-schemas-1217.md) — the C6 schema spec (MVP slice) for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): the **data schema of each of the six visual primitives** — what each consumes (a real `file:line` witnessed source), its shape (time-series / roll-up / heatmap, **never a single point**), and the cross-check (A/B/C/D) it carries — riding a shared `CtxSafetyPanel` / `PanelPoint` envelope that reuses the `internal/covmatrix:33` `Schema = "fak-coverage-matrix/1"` versioned-payload precedent, the `internal/scoreboard/render.go:41` `FromPayload` text/emoji fallback, and the `internal/cdb/report_html.go:91` `(*Image).HTMLReport` HTML precedent. The six: **(1)** event ribbon (journal `CAP_EVICT`/`CAP_FAULT` + `cacheevents.go` `CacheEventRecorder` + `cachemeta/kvtransfer.go:34-48` `KVTransfer` ok/missed/fault), **(2)** saved-vs-realized gap (C4), **(3)** S/N+Faults strip (`signalnoise.go:69/:81/:249`), **(4)** evict-correctness heatmap (`kvcache.go:44-105` + `recall.PageSyndrome`), **(5)** residency conservation bar (`ctxresidency.go:16-31` `State` + `:39-42` `EvictBlastRadius`), **(6)** liveness light (`fak_bgloop_up` vs decode-rate). The envelope structurally forbids a single trust-me point (every point carries a paired axis, a conservation segment, a provenance lane, and a re-derivability bit). Schemas doctrine A–D of the C1 note (#1218); renders the C2 failures (#1219); rendering *home* is C11 (#1229). Research/design only.
- [Context-safety re-derivation checker (#1227, C9 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-rederivation-checker-1217.md) — the C9 **keystone** spec (MVP slice) for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217) — the genuinely missing piece the doctrine names. Specs the **re-derivation checker**: the contract under which a rendered context-safety visual is **RED unless every number on it re-derives from a tamper-evident source**. Today rendering is downstream (Grafana over `/metrics`, Jekyll over scorecard JSON) and **never re-validates after render** (C2 gap G-A). Generalizes the in-tree **rebuild-and-prove-equal** discipline — `internal/ctxplan/image.go:61-76` proves `RestoreIndex(ix.Image()) == ix` for the *index* (`image_test.go:18` `TestIndexImageRoundTripIsIdentity`) — from the index to the **rendered visual** (the one analog the tree lacks). Enumerates the tamper-evident sources the checker is restricted to (the hash-chained journal `journal.go` `Verify`/`VerifyRows` `:577`/`:619`; the WITNESSED `/metrics` family; git via `dos commit-audit`; disk CAS digests via `recall.PageSyndromeFor`), the `RederivationVerdict` / `NumberCheck` contract (every number checked, GREEN only on equality-within-tolerance against a tamper-evident re-derivation, one RED/REFUSED number reds the whole visual), and the structured refusal a non-re-derivable number emits instead of an unearned OK (`SAFETY_UNRECOVERED` / `VALUE_UNRECONCILED` / `SAFETY_UNWITNESSED`, C13 #1231). Lifts four shipped precedents (`image.go`, journal `Verify`, `check_memory.py`, `dispatch_status.py` strict diff-witnessed, the `metrics.go` `proven` vCache gate). CI-gate sibling is C10 (#1228). Research/design only.
- [Context-safety reuse-correctness witness (#1232, C14 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-reuse-correctness-witness-1217.md) — the C14 second-derivation spec for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): the reuse-**correctness** witness that the C4 saved-vs-realized reuse **count** must reconcile against, so a high reuse count over a *broken* prefix is caught as value that only looks real. Binds two existing fail-closed `internal/cachemeta` verdicts — `prefix_coherence.go:51` `EvaluatePrefixCoherence(...) PrefixBreakDirective` (uncertainty → break the prefix, never an optimistic "probably fine") + `prefix_stability.go:193` `StabilityReport` (produced by `AnalyzeStability` `:203`) — as the second derivation, and states the reconciliation rule `Reconciled ⟺ (RealizedReused == 0) ∨ (Coherent ∧ Stable)`: a non-zero realized-reuse count is credited only if the reused prefix is coherent AND stable, else the gap panel refuses green with `VALUE_UNRECONCILED` (C13). - [Context-safety DOS refusal tokens (#1231, C13 of epic #1217) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/context-safety-dos-refusal-tokens-1217.md) — the C13 structured-refusal spec for the context-safety epic [#1217](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1217): the three new `dos.toml [reasons]` tokens a panel emits to **refuse green with a verifiable reason** instead of rendering an unearned OK — `SAFETY_UNRECOVERED` (a context-removal event with no tamper-evident journal row), `VALUE_UNRECONCILED` (the reuse count credits value the C14 coherence/stability witness refutes), `SAFETY_UNWITNESSED` (a rendered number with no tamper-evident source). Witnessed gap as the anchor: all three return `known=false, UNCLASSIFIED` via `dos_check_reason` today, so a panel cannot emit them until declared; the TOML sketch matches the real `[reasons.*]` grammar (`dos.toml:424/445`). The refusal vocabulary the C9 checker (#1227) + C4 gap (#1221) + C14 reconciliation (#1232) emit. Research/design only.

### Concepts, benchmarks & run logs

- [The agent programming grammar — lifting fak's invariants into a domain-free substrate (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-AGENT-PROGRAMMING-GRAMMAR-2026-06-28.md) — the "express + generalize" half of the innovations survey: fak's contribution is one invariant (*a decision no participant can move by narrating a number*) carried at every scale, not any single primitive (0/29 novel). Extracts that invariant as a reusable **grammar** — nouns (lane, lease, reason token, witness, verdict, claim, ladder rung, scope) and verbs (arbitrate, verify, audit, review, refuse, recall, resolve, status) — names the ~10 fak concepts already lifted into the domain-free DOS form, the two structural shapes a correct primitive obeys (the verification ladder; the security==optimization two lenses), and scopes the **under-expressed** concepts (`G1–G9`: readiness ladder, verification-ladder verb, durability-class promotion, materialized-view context contract, prediction-vs-reality calibration, one-sided-screen polarity, taint-check, per-aspect routing, net-true-value claim-check) as the next grammar verbs. The companion of the durable [innovations index](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/INNOVATIONS-INDEX.md); actioned by the grammar epic.
- [The feature-maturity lifecycle ladder — completeness is not maturity, and every gap is the next work item (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-MATURITY-LADDER-2026-06-29.md) — the **shipped** subsystem for the long-horizon "agentic culture" problem: a v1 prototype can be legitimately *complete* yet not tested, not dogfooded, not benchmarked, not the default — and the operator should SEE where each capability sits and what would mature it next. [`internal/maturity`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/tree/main/internal/maturity) places every declared fak capability (one per `internal/<leaf>` lane in [`dos.toml`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/dos.toml) `[lanes.trees]`) on a closed lifecycle ladder — `proposed → prototyped → tested → dogfooded → default` (with a `benchmarked` badge) — each rung gated by evidence the author did not write (code on disk, a `*_test.go`, an edge in the running binary's transitive import graph, a documented verb), so a rung moves only by changing the real tree. **Immaturity is never a defect** (a complete v1 honestly sitting at `prototyped` is expected); the one thing it refuses is a **ladder-skip** — a capability fak relies on yet leaves untested (`maturity_debt`, the maturity sibling of the readiness ladder's `READINESS_OVERCLAIM`). For each capability the first unmet rung is rendered as a concrete **next work item**, and `fak maturity next` is the ranked backlog the issue-dispatch loop pulls from — the mechanization of "each agent has the desire to create the next ticket." The shipped fak-tree binding of grammar [G1 / the readiness ladder](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-AGENT-PROGRAMMING-GRAMMAR-2026-06-28.md); first dogfood run over fak's own 109 lanes: index 78/100, 0 ladder-skips, 18 tested-but-not-dogfooded.
- [Complain by default — the agentic-dev friction channels and when to use each (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-AGENT-FRICTION-COMPLAINT-CHANNELS-2026-06-29.md) — a playbook for the `/goal` "improve the default ability for agents to complain about annoying agentic-dev things": friction that no agent records stays trapped in per-agent private memory and is re-discovered by the next agent, so the default response to a papercut should be to register it through a structured, **deduplicating** channel that is part of the repo. Names a closed, evidence-grounded **friction taxonomy** (`shared-tree-clobber`, `red-trunk`, `stamp-refusal`, `push-blocked`, `saturated-box`, `tool-timeout`, `lane-collision`, `guard-false-positive`, `confusing-refusal`, `phantom-artifact`) and routes each to the channel that fits *who acts and how fast* — operator/status surfacing via `fak blockers post|feed` (shipped), the capability-floor **appeal** that must carry the witnessed journal verdict (`internal/guardcomplaint`; the `fak complain` dispatch is `not yet` wired — mid-rework on the shared tree), the DOS closed **refusal vocabulary** (`dos_refuse_reasons`/`dos_check_reason`) to decline green with a verifiable reason, and the `internal/dogfoodissues` dedup/escalate fold for recurring process friction. Four rules for complaining as signal not noise (structured+deduped, carry a witness not a feeling, name the recovery you wanted, route by who acts). Companion of the [agent programming grammar](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-AGENT-PROGRAMMING-GRAMMAR-2026-06-28.md); the `not yet` half (wire the verb + a `workflow`/`dev` domain) is the next checkable step.
- [Affordable-hardware agent fleets — the doable tier, and what shows it (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/AFFORDABLE-HARDWARE-AGENT-FLEETS-2026-06-28.md) — a strategy/framing + showable-demo map for running **multiple** coding agents **safely** on hardware a small team can afford (one big-RAM CPU box, one or a few older datacenter GPU/Ampere GPUs, a gaming GPU, or a Mac), including overnight/offline. Thesis: the agent fleet is the workload where affordable hardware wins, because it is latency-tolerant (batch it overnight), prefix-heavy (pay the setup once), and unattended (so trust, not tok/s, binds). Separates the **witnessed-today** tier (sub-frontier ≤27B — the 27B @64–128-concurrency curve, the 4070 862-agg-tok/s batch, the Mac 4.1× fleet stack, the 1,024-agent CPU `fanrun`, the GPU-free `fleet-reuse-demo`) from the **honest not-yet** (frontier 753B GLM-5.2 on CPU-offload at sub-1 tok/s — the #971 host-expert wall; TPU = no backend), and ties each tier to the specific fak lever (RadixAttention prefix reuse, continuous batching, resident-Q4_K, capacity preflight) and safety rail (default-deny capabilities, `dos_arbitrate` disjoint lanes, commit-audit, quarantine) that makes it usable. Every measured number cited to its authority row; every projection labeled.
- [Desktop slowness maintenance runbook — sprawl, not resources, on the fleet workstation (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/DESKTOP-SLOWNESS-MAINTENANCE-2026-06-28.md) — why the workstation "feels slow" is not resource exhaustion (CPU ~32%, RAM 25% used, disk queue 0, no thermal throttle) but two reboot-cleared accumulations: one WindowsTerminal rendering all fleet panes (2.2 GB / 14.7k handles) and a growing TermService/RDP handle leak (2.5 → 3.0 GB within a single session). Records the reboot cadence, the Defender build-tree exclusion command, and the verified do-NOT list (do not bulk-kill "idle" python/pwsh — they are live DOS-MCP/session workers, classified by parent liveness; do not clear the shared ~18 GB go-build cache).
- [D-006 (#243) Tool Ecosystem Expansion — architecture-fit decision + honest status (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/D-006-TOOL-ECOSYSTEM-ARCH-FIT-243-2026-06-28.md) — discharges the [#304 tracker](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/track-d-agent-framework-parity-tracking-304.md)'s deferred "decide the architecture fit first" step for [#243](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/243): fak's tool ecosystem is **gate-native, not provider-native**. - [fak guard SECRET_EXFIL audit — banner clarity + version build-provenance (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/AUDIT-fak-guard-secret-exfil-2026-06-28.md) — the audit behind 06179a0c: the SECRET_EXFIL quarantine banner is current HEAD behavior (default-on normgate), not a stale binary; `fak version` now stamps the binary's VCS revision so a stale binary is detectable; the inbound-quarantine banner was rewritten to plain-language, non-alarming text. - [Two cache stacks, one wire — fak's cache concepts vs the agent harness's, and do we disable Claude Code auto-compaction? (#1131) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/HARNESS-CACHE-COHERENCE-AUDIT-2026-06-28.md) — audit of the coherence between fak's cache/context machinery (cache-preserving compaction #745, budget reset / cut-vs-reset #774, prompt-MMU #751, ctxmmu quarantine, paged-KV evict, cachemeta prefix-stability/coherence) and the agent harness's OWN machinery (Claude Code auto-compaction, `cache_control` prompt-cache, ~5-min TTL). Names the interference matrix: the two managers stack blind to each other — fak is cache-**preserving**, the harness's auto-compaction is cache-**destroying** (it rewrites the `cache_control` prefix, bursting the cache fak just preserved) and can defeat a quarantine by folding a sealed span into its summary. Answers the explicit question with evidence: Claude Code auto-compaction **cannot be reliably disabled via settings/env** (the toggle is silently ignored; threshold clamped ~83%; anthropics/claude-code #38483/#42817/#42149) — the one dependable lever is a **`PreCompact` hook (exit 2)**, so the answer is a conditional protocol (**block** while fak copes, **allow** when fak's compaction bails, **reset** past TTL), not a flag flip. Lands the spine [`internal/compactcohere`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/internal/compactcohere/compactcohere.go): a pure tier-1 sensor that attributes a per-turn prefix event (`stable`/`fak_cut`/`fak_world_break`/`harness_rewrite`/`cold_ttl`) + a standing block/allow PreCompact posture, reusing `cachemeta` divergence rather than duplicating it. Actuators (gateway wiring, the guard hook, the quarantine-survival witness) are the epic.
- [Ultracode dogfood — a 9-agent fleet advancing Qwen3.6 parity (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/ULTRACODE-DOGFOOD-QWEN36-PARITY-2026-06-28.md) — a measured session record of fak's *ultracode* (multi-agent) mode run as two concurrent waves (4 production + 5 verification agents on disjoint file lanes) against the Qwen3.6-27B-vs-llama.cpp parity goal: 8 independent reviewed deliverables, ~48 min of agent labor compressed into ~20 min agent-phase wall-clock (**2.38× wall-clock / 8× deliverable-count**), with the agent-orchestration multiple fenced strictly apart from fak's separate **inference** 5–10x (different axis, cited never blended). - [Evict-on-paged KV — the bit-exact middle-span Evict survives a block-paged layout (#33) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/EVICT-ON-PAGED-KV-DESIGN-2026-06-28.md) — design + prototype proof for [#33](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/33) (the gate before the native paged allocator [#34](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/34) and the L3 governance referee [#27](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/27)). Verdict **GO**: fak's kernel-owned, bit-exact middle-span `KVCache.Evict` carries forward onto a block-paged layout because the single-rotation re-RoPE of a shifted survivor depends only on its pre-RoPE `Kraw` and its **new logical position**, not on physical contiguity. Two requirements proven on real float32 KV with no GPU: the paged blocks must carry a per-token `Kraw` plane (the shipped #277 allocator stored only K/V — `NewPagedKVPoolWithRaw` adds it), and a survivor re-RoPE must copy-on-write-split any shared block before mutating K. A mid-span evict on a deliberately non-contiguous page table is **byte-for-byte identical** to the contiguous `Evict` (cache **and** next-token logits, `max|Δ|=0` on amd64), and a COW-forked sibling is left untouched (`internal/model/paged_evict.go`, `internal/model/paged_evict_test.go`). Names the honest cost (an intra-block compaction on middle-span evict, which vLLM/SGLang avoid only because they cannot evict a middle span at all), the FP8/INT8-KV decision (keep `Kraw` f32 per [#1047](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/1047); defer quantized-K-with-exact-span), and scopes the GLM-DSA path out with reason (its `glm.rerotateSurvivor` follows the identical new-logical-index re-derivation; carrying the DSA state onto blocks is #34's job).
- [`L3RegionBackend` — child B of epic #79, designed behind the frozen `Ref`/`Resolver`/`RegionBackend` seam (#55) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/L3REGIONBACKEND-CHILD-B-DESIGN-55-2026-06-28.md) — the `design(` artifact for [#55](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/55) (Option B): the interface, span→page-key contract, resolve/page-in/page-out/evict lifecycle, G2 middle-eviction fold, and G3 deletion-certificate tier-projection that unlock **G2** (evict a poisoned span from the *middle* of pages shared across sequences) and native **G3** (attest the *L3 pages* were destroyed, not just the local copy) — neither reachable from a control-path-only sidecar. Specifies `L3RegionBackend` as a **backend swap** under the frozen `abi.RegionBackend` seam (`internal/abi/registry.go:609`) with **no ABI edit**, each method named against the external store's `mget`/`mset`/evict, the per-page `Ref.Digest` verify stated as a **fail-closed** page-in admission gate (G1), `evict(from,n)` mapped through fak-owned `KVCache.Evict` re-rotation (bit-exact `max|Δ|=0` survivors) to an L3 page-key delete + re-key, and `deletioncert.Mint` folded to attest the L3 page-key set offline-verifiably. Honest spine: the in-kernel engine (v0.2) OR a co-residence handshake is a **HARD [GAP] ~120h-class precondition**, the design stays on the **control path** (§6.5: opt-in admission verify, not an inline per-RDMA-read byte-scan; ~1–5 µs L3 read budget named), the staged plan gates run on a **mock/local** L3 (real-store wire optional/follow-on), it composes with [#493](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/493) (network `StageTransport`) for the multi-node case, and the whole backend is **gated behind Option A** (the referee sidecar) proving the seam first. The design row [`L3-DISAGGREGATED-CACHE-REIMAGINED`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/L3-DISAGGREGATED-CACHE-REIMAGINED.md) (epic [#79](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/79)) labelled "child B".

Proposes the ladder: P1 turn-boundary witnessed journal (extends [#636](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/636)), P2 residual meter + `KILL_SAFE` verdict (measure *unrecorded* window state, not window fullness), P3 restart-parity probe (a referee that grades "this checkpoint suffices to resume" instead of trusting it), P4 witnessed promotion gate into shared memory (truth-duration + provenance + recall-time re-verification end to end), P5 memory tree as an arbitrated dos lane, P6 heal the forked store. Each rung carries its next checkable step; §7 fences the model-relative residual definition and the shallow-parity failure mode.
