- [The readiness / durability verdict ladder as a domain-free DOS primitive (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-DOS-READINESS-VERDICT-LADDER-2026-06-26.md) — concept capture for [#582](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/582): the mechanism behind the product scorecard ([`tools/product_scorecard.py`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/tools/product_scorecard.py) / [PRODUCT-STATUS](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/PRODUCT-STATUS.md)) is not fak-specific — it is a generic DOS primitive. A **closed maturity ladder** (`durable-product → … → concept-only`) where every rung's promotion is gated by **evidence the claimant did not author** (the CLAIMS tag a concept carries, whether its first command resolves to a real `cmd/` dir + documented verb, whether its witness/entry docs exist on disk), plus a **surface-ceiling gate** that stops a benchmark from posing as a durable product and a stub from posing as shipped — so a verdict can only move by changing the real tree, never the data. The note (1) extracts the surface-gate + evidence-binding core into a domain-free five-part form (closed rung vocabulary, surface→ceiling cap, capability set, evidence predicates over ground truth, evidence-bound adjudication with overclaim-refusal), (2) sketches a `dos`-grounded variant where the top rung is closed by a `dos` **witness** (`dos_verify` reads git ancestry, `dos_commit_audit` separates a `diff-witnessed` claim from a forgeable `subject-only` one) and an overclaim is refused with a structured reason from a closed vocabulary (cf. `dos_refuse_reasons`, proposed token `READINESS_OVERCLAIM`), and (3) decides where it lives: **keep the tree-cross-check shell a fak tool, lift the closed-ladder + ceiling-gate + evidence-bound-adjudication + refusal core into the DOS concept vocabulary** — building a `dos readiness` verb is a dos-kernel follow-up named as the next step, not committed here (the issue scoped this to concept capture, no code).
- [One machine: the session lifecycle IS serving admission (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SESSION-LIFECYCLE-IS-SERVING-ADMISSION-2026-06-26.md) — explores the parallel between session start/resume and dynamic fused serving of random-length, flexible-turn sessions. The thesis: the `internal/session` run-state machine (start/throttle/pause/drain/stop + cold `Restore` + `Recontinue`) and the continuous-batch serving operation (admit/preempt/evict/resume a sequence) are **one state machine at two altitudes**, with the agent **turn boundary** as the single admission/preemption/resume quantum. fak already implies this but spells the machine twice (`session.RunState` vs `loopmgr.LoopState`, two enums sharing `paused/draining/stopped`) and only advisory-couples the halves (`TurnIntent` is consumed by prewarm/discard admission but gates no live served batch). Maps the verified correspondence (session verb ↔ serving verb ↔ status ↔ grounding symbol), separates the buildable seams (shared vocabulary, one epoch lineage, `SlotEvent`→KV reclaim, warm-swap on resume) from the analogy-only rows (cross-host live migration; `KVIncluded=false` by design), positions against prior art ([#805](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/805)/[#748](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/748)/[#637](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/637)/[#809](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/809)/[#844](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/844)), and proposes the unification epic [#912](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/912) (children [#913](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/913)–[#916](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/916)). Decomposition adversarially verified by a multi-agent workflow; every cited file:symbol and issue state confirmed against the tree.
- [Is witnessed span-attention a valid reward? Verdict, aggregation, and failure modes (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-witnessed-span-attention-validity-2026-06-26.md) — prior-art survey 1/5 for the reward-over-spans epic [#860](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/860): the attention-as-explanation debate resolved into a usable rule for [#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861). Verdict: witnessed span-attention is a cheap, relative, span-level proposal signal, not a standalone causal explanation or accepted reward until it correlates with exact-eviction leave-one-out. The note maps Jain/Wallace, Wiegreffe/Pinter, Serrano/Smith, and Abnar/Zuidema to fak's actual post-softmax observer and span ledger, then pins the aggregation rule: consumer rows only, span-level mass, all observed heads/layers summed for direct cache-read accounting, position/length normalization, and top/bottom LOO validation before any live planner or RSI promotion. Satisfies [#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861).
- [Span-attention confound normalization: sinks, position, recency, and length (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-span-attention-confound-normalization-2026-06-26.md) — prior-art survey 2/5 for the reward-over-spans epic [#860](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/860): the normalization contract for [#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862). Raw attention is demoted to telemetry unless `expected_attention_mass` subtracts sink/preamble positions, massive-activation/outlier token effects, span length, relative-position/U-shaped long-context bias, and distance-to-query/recency defaults. The note defines the null-model rungs (uniform-visible fallback, position-length baseline, distance/age baseline, sink mask, per-head/layer calibration) and maps them to `SpanRewardSegment.ExpectedAttentionMass`, `NormalizedReward`, and `ConfoundNormalizationImproved`, preserving the rule that exact-eviction LOO decides whether the residual attention actually mattered. Satisfies [#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862).
- [Span-reward novelty boundary: H2O, ContextCite, PRMs, and the defensible claim (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-span-reward-novelty-boundary-2026-06-26.md) — prior-art synthesis 5/5 for the reward-over-spans epic [#860](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/860): the honest novelty boundary against H2O/SnapKV/Quest, ContextCite, influence methods, and PRMs. The defensible claim is a witnessed, replayable, falsifiable span-credit proxy, not "attention proves causality"; the note lists the exact fak deltas, the H2O-with-new-names dimensions, and the forbidden overclaims downstream docs must avoid. Satisfies [#865](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/865).
- [Span-credit signal menu: attention, gradients, leave-one-out, influence, and the fak fallback (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-span-credit-signal-menu-2026-06-26.md) — prior-art survey 3/5 for the reward-over-spans epic [#860](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/860): ranks candidate context-span credit signals by faithfulness times cost, with the recommended design for [#863](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/863): attention is a cheap proposal distribution, exact-eviction leave-one-out verifies the top/bottom candidates, and `CORRELATE` / `REFUTE` / `INSUFFICIENT` decides whether attention may be promoted, replaced by LOO deltas, or held for more evidence. The note maps Integrated Gradients, Grad x Input, occlusion, influence functions, TracIn, ContextCite, and the attention-explanation debate onto fak's shipped `span_reward_shadow` and `ctxplan` seams, while preserving the overclaim fence that no live planner/RSI flip happens until #866 proves correlation against the eviction witness. Satisfies [#863](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/863).
- [Mac Qwen3.6-27B Metal Q4_K perf diagnosis: decode 1.2 / prefill 0.6 tok/s, the per-call command-buffer wall (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/MAC-QWEN36-27B-Q4K-METAL-PERF-DIAGNOSIS-2026-06-26.md) — a clean on-device measurement (M3 Pro, `-tags fakmetal`, `FAK_Q4K=1 FAK_METAL=1`, llama-server stopped) of fak's resident-Q4_K Metal path for the big Mac model, toward the 3× decode goal. The kernels are **bit-correct** (q4k GEMV cosine 1.000000, greedy token-parity vs CPU, both green on-box) but throughput is **0.16× of SOTA**: decode 1.2 tok/s vs llama.cpp-Metal 7.29, prefill 0.6 vs 51.55. `FAK_QPROFILE` phase profiles + the `q4k_gemv`/`q4k_gemm` microbench locate the wall precisely — each decode token issues ~336 *separate* Metal command-buffer GEMVs (≈7 matmuls × ~48–64 layers) and an isolated GEMV is **~360 µs launch/sync-bound** on top of ~98 µs of actual work (GEMV 32 GB/s ≈21% bandwidth; GEMM 364 GFLOP/s ≈5% FLOP). Re-prioritizes epic [#59](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/59): the kernel children (#515 q4_k GEMM / #516 resident weights / #517 decode GEMV / #71 hybrid prefill) have effectively **landed**, so the binding levers are now [#67](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/67) (one MTLCommandBuffer per forward — the GPU-resident decode forward, decode twin of the shipped `mg_prefill`) and a kernel-efficiency pass. Witness: `experiments/benchmark/runs/by-machine/node-macos-a/20260626T055239Z-q4k-metal-decode-27b/score.json`.
- [Mac Qwen2.5-7B Q8 GPU-resident decode forward: at performant parity with llama.cpp-Metal (0.99×) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/MAC-QWEN25-7B-Q8-RESIDENT-DECODE-2026-06-26.md) — the [#67](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/67) one-command-buffer GPU-resident **dense Q8 decode forward** (the decode twin of the shipped `mg_prefill`), built, optimized and measured on the M3 Pro. **Correct** — logit cosine **0.999991** + greedy token-parity vs the CPU Q8 decode (`TestMetalDecodeResidentMatchesCPU`), and the real Qwen2.5-1.5B Q8 emits the same text as CPU (`"...France is" -> "Paris"`); engages on Qwen2.5-7B Q8 with attention bias. **Six shipped optimizations took clean 7B Q8 decode 10.0 -> 17.6 tok/s (0.56× -> 0.988× of llama.cpp-Metal 17.82) — AT PARITY** (within ~1.2%, inside run-to-run variance): a **parallel RMSNorm** (the v0 ran the H-wide norm on ONE GPU thread ×56/token — a matmul-only split found it; +0.24×), the **LM head + final norm on the GPU** (+0.08×), **f16 block scales** + fused bias (GGUF Q8_0 std, ~6% fewer bytes; +0.04×), **persistent on-GPU KV** (seed once, append in place; +0.025×), and **key-parallel flash-decode attention** (8 simdgroups/head split the keys + flash-combine — a skip-attention split isolated the serial O(ctx) attention as the last residual; +0.04×). fak's projection GEMVs already run at **~154 GB/s, ABOVE llama's ~143**, and the matmul+head floor (~55.5 ms) is below llama's full decode (~56.1 ms). Shipped `5a11a31`..`d6188182`. Continues [MAC-QWEN36-27B-Q4K-METAL-PERF-DIAGNOSIS](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/MAC-QWEN36-27B-Q4K-METAL-PERF-DIAGNOSIS-2026-06-26.md).
- [idea-scout triage: out-of-band injection-defense taxonomy + adaptive evaluation (#909) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-out-of-band-injection-defense-taxonomy-triage-2026-06-26.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26479 (Narisetty/Kore/Kattamanchi/Kumarapu, "Adaptive Evaluation of Out-of-Band Defenses Against Prompt Injection in LLM Agents"): the **survey that names fak's own family** — defend a tool-using agent against indirect prompt injection NOT by training the model to refuse but by enforcing security *outside* the model with a deterministic policy that mediates its actions (CaMeL/FIDES/Progent/RTBAS/FORGE), organized as classical **reference monitoring + Biba integrity + least privilege**. Verdict: **prior art to cite** — fak IS an out-of-band defense (default-deny capability floor = reference monitor + least privilege, IFC `Ref.Taint` sink-gating = Biba integrity, result-admit quarantine = containment that holds when the model is fooled), so the taxonomy is the academic name for the seams [`docs/industry-scorecard/security.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/industry-scorecard/security.md) already calls "FIDES/CaMeL-class". The paper's second contribution — every one of these defenses is validated only on **static** benchmarks, the same methodology that made in-band defenses look strong until adaptive attacks broke twelve at >90% — independently backs fak's deliberate non-load-bearing-detection bet (~100% evadable, by design) while **raising the bar** fak's own `internal/agentdojo` ASR battery should meet (adaptive, defense-aware, not static); the paper's own adaptive result is one small black-box data point (Progent on AgentDojo, Qwen2.5-7B/H200, mean ASR 25.8%→4.2%, adaptive 2.6%, white-box GCG still open), cited as a protocol to adopt for evaluation, never as evidence fak's containment is adaptively robust. No capability adopted (fak already enforces out-of-band); not a threat (a parallel defense on fak's side of the trust boundary). Resolved by `e7a6607`.
- [Compaction vs. the industry: drop-and-splice vs summarize-and-resend (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/COMPACTION-VS-INDUSTRY-2026-06-25.md) — a sourced audit of how fak's cache-prefix-preserving history compaction differs from the built-in compaction in Claude Code, the Anthropic API context-editing feature, Cursor, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Aider, and LangChain. Industry mechanisms web-sourced; every fak claim adversarially verified against `internal/agent/anthropic_compact.go` and the gateway. The crux: almost everyone summarizes/clears and re-sends a **rewritten** prompt (which the providers' own docs say breaks the prompt cache); fak drops middle turns and **byte-splices** so the cached prefix stays byte-identical (`bytes.Equal` proven, 13 fail-safe identity exits). Records the four disambiguations that survived adversarial review — the provider cache **cascade** is an unverified hypothesis not a measured fact (the audit's biggest open risk; the `/metrics` instrument exists, it needs one credentialed Anthropic session, [#745](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/745)); fak vs Anthropic context-editing is **orthogonal** (cache-preservation vs recoverable tool-result clearing), not "better"; "lossless" is **overloaded** → a four-axis table (cache-bytes / trust-boundary / model-context / recoverability); Anthropic-wire-shaped **by implementation, not necessity**. Adds the durable surface: a new `client-compaction` dimension in the industry scorecard (a categorical byte-splice **lead** row + an explicit **no-claim** on realized cache reuse).
- [idea-scout triage: attention-located malicious-skill detection (#771) (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-malicious-agent-skills-attention-triage-2026-06-25.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.23416 ("Detecting Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild using Attention", Etteib/Lunghi/Bissyandé): marketplace skills run with user privileges, and the paper's load-bearing claim is that prompt-injection defenses collapse because a skill *is* instructions (the trusted/untrusted-data boundary disappears). Its **Locate-and-Judge** detector scores skill spans by instruction-following **attention** and judges only top-K, auditing a marketplace at order-of-magnitude lower cost. Verdict: **prior art to cite** — it independently validates *why* fak gates the **capability** a skill exercises rather than classifying its instructions (exactly the boundary the paper shows collapses) — plus a real threat whose action step (exfiltrate=send, hijack=destructive call, persist=write) fak's default-deny capability floor already gates a layer **below** a static pre-load scanner. The attention-locator is **not adopted** (best-effort, no kernel load surface, and its attention-is-importance premise is what fak's own [#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861)/[#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862) is still auditing).
- [fak in-kernel CUDA serve on an L4: live tok/s + a concurrency crash fixed (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/L4-INKERNEL-SERVE-AND-CONCURRENCY-FIX-2026-06-25.md) — the reachable-hardware companion to the [GPU server cross-engine](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/GPU-SERVER-CROSS-ENGINE-DATA-2026-06-25.md) note: with the 8-GPU server nodes reachable only through a down private control bridge, this records what could be measured on the one live GPU node (the `fak-realmodel` GCP L4). Two results. (1) The first **warm steady-state** decode rate against fak's *live* in-kernel CUDA serve: a real Qwen2.5-0.5B Q8_0 decodes at **~466 tok/s** single-stream (median of 8, range 437–510; ~2.25 GB of 23 GB VRAM) — an order of magnitude over the WSL-laptop Q8 numbers, confirming [GPU-QWEN-RESULTS](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/GPU-QWEN-RESULTS.md)'s thesis that the laptop gap was the WSL launch tax, not the kernel (the *cold* first decode is ~66 tok/s and must not be quoted as steady-state). (2) The serving bug live traffic exposed: a concurrent `/v1/messages` burst **took the GPU serve down** — the single-stream CUDA backend (one `g_stream`, one cuBLAS handle, a shared device free-list) was driven by two concurrent `InKernelPlanner.Complete` goroutines whose per-token op sequences interleaved and corrupted each other's device buffers → sticky `cuda_kernels.cu` illegal-memory-access → poisoned context until restart (the sibling **CPU** serve answered correctly throughout, isolating the fault). Fixed by holding a dedicated `devMu` across the whole forward when a backend is wired (safe queuing, correct for a single-stream device; CPU path untouched), with a **proven non-vacuous** GPU-free test (3719 op-overlaps without the lock, 0 with it). Honestly scoped: a small-model device-decode serving rate, not a 753B / GPU server / stock-engine number.
- [Credit assignment over spans: PRMs, RL credit, agent-memory usefulness (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-credit-assignment-over-spans-2026-06-25.md) — prior-art survey 4/5 for the reward-over-spans epic [#860](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/860): how the RL / agent-training literature assigns credit to intermediate steps and retrieved items, and the span-credit-assignment design those patterns produce. Folds four families into one reward equation — `reward(s,T) = success_gate(T) · Σ γ^(T−t) · m_s(t)` — with each term justified by a named pattern (**outcome gate** from PRMs / Math-Shepherd; **recency discount** from TD(λ) eligibility traces / GAE; **confound normalization** from attention-sink + the "attention is/is-not explanation" contest) and each mapped onto a fak seam that already ships (`ctxplan.OutcomeFromAttention` produces it, `Forecast.Learn` / `Weights.Learn` consume it into the `recall.Page.Utility` Q-slot, `rsiloop` keeps-or-reverts on witnessed signal/noise). Every term is **degenerate-to-current** (identity knobs reproduce the shipped flat cumulative attention) so [#866](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/866) can ablate each independently; carries the epic's honest spine verbatim — attention-as-importance is **contested**, so the producer is a swap point that takes the leave-one-out signal ([#863](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/863)) at the same `Outcome` interface if validation refutes attention, and the outcome gate demands a **witnessed** verdict, never the model's self-report.
- [Shared live trunk vs. branch / worktree / VM-per-agent (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SHARED-TRUNK-VS-PER-AGENT-ISOLATION-2026-06-25.md) — the positioning half of epic [#822](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/822) / [#834](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/834): the field (Cursor background agents, Devin, Sculptor, OpenHands, Dagger `container-use`, Google GitFarm) converged on **never share a tree** — branch/worktree/VM per agent, integration gated on a human merge. That validates fak's contrarian bet (one **live trunk** + **pre-call adjudication** + **disjoint-lease admission**) while giving it **nothing to import** for the hard part, because every surveyed system *avoids* the shared-tree problem rather than solving it. Names the trade as a table (what each side buys/costs), the three named git-admin gaps with their current closure status at HEAD, and carries the epic's honesty caveats **verbatim**: `mvdan/sh` cannot resolve `$VAR`/`alias`/`eval` (fail closed); `grite` = distribution **not** atomicity + the **synthetic** "78%→0%"; a signature is an **identity envelope only** (the SHA already content-addresses); AgenticFlict **sizes the problem, never claims fak's benefit**.
- [Fusion, ref-counting, and GC for the agent loop (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/FUSION-REFCOUNT-GC-FOR-THE-AGENT-LOOP-2026-06-25.md) — the runtime-heap lens on the loop: every turn and tool result is a **heap object**, a pinned goal / active slash-command / open task is a **GC root**, compaction is **garbage collection**. The decisive finding after mapping the tree: the collector machine already ships at the byte/KV depths (`abi.CASPinner` refcount-by-digest, `ProvisionalSink.Promote/Rollback` commit-or-collect, `ctxplan.Forecast.Pins` whose own doc names "the active goal" as the canonical pin, `cachemeta.Lifecycle` TTL+`Touch`-revive) — what is missing is the single **edge from an intentional root to the heap objects it keeps alive**. Locates the gap exactly at `SessionPlanner.pins()` (the complete current root-set is system/first-user/last-user; the goal is absent), defines the **ref-count of a turn** (its live referents: an open goal, a later citing turn, a pending consumer), the conservative over-retain safety asymmetry (a false-free silently loses needed context; a false-retain costs a few tokens), **turn-fusion** (collapse a refcount-1 producer→consumer intermediate, the sound version of `maybeCompactInboundTools`) and **command-tenuring** (a recurring slash-command promotes to a compact rollup — the "store it for aggregate/GC" the goal asked for), and a 4-step first build that wires the goal into the per-turn pin set and measures the effect on the shipped signal/noise metric.
- [vToolcall, forked — best-effort serve-tiers and owning the loop (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/VTOOLCALL-FORK-AND-BESTEFFORT-2026-06-25.md) — the forward-looking sequel to the materialized-view note, answering "best effort" + "fork an open harness (Crush / opencode)". Adds (1) a **consistency-level QoS axis** (`STRICT | BOUNDED_STALE | BEST_EFFORT | SPECULATIVE` threaded as `c.Meta["consistency"]`, a DB-read-consistency dual) with a per-topology graceful-degradation capability matrix, and (2) the **fork direction**: make fak the tool *dispatcher* so the prior note's "impossible on the proxy" verdict flips and serve-as-ran runs closed-loop on real built-in tools. Honest spine, all three stated plainly: forking does not *soften* un-ring, it **relocates** it (after-consumption → a before-consumption write barrier fak owns, needing a net-new suspend-and-resume turn primitive — today's `gateTurn` only terminates); **Crush is FSL-1.1-MIT** (source-available, commercial-restricted at HEAD) so the license-clean call is **build the minimal native TUI on the shipped `internal/agent` seam** (Apache-uniform, single-binary) or host **opencode-as-server** (MIT), never fork Crush into the Apache module; and the loop fak would extend is a **benchmark A/B comparator (`RunArm`) today**, not a production loop. Portfolio verdict: keep the proxy as the universal gate, lead the fork with the native build.
- [vToolcall — tool results as a materialized view (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/VTOOLCALL-MATERIALIZED-VIEW-2026-06-25.md) — the *closed-loop* dual of [vCache](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/VCACHE-VIRTUAL-API-CACHE-2026-06-24.md): serve a tool result from the kernel's own cache **as if the tool ran**, framed as one materialized view in a query engine over the whole harness-facing surface (tool-defs via `promptmmu`, history via `agent.CompactAnthropicHistory`, context via `contextq`, KV via vCache — and now results via the vDSO). The serve mechanism already ships as the vDSO FastPath (`kernel.go:347` → `abi.FastPaths().Lookup`); this note is its design rationale with **cache invalidation as the spine**. Honest build boundary: result-synthesis is real only where fak *dispatches* the tool (`fak_syscall`/in-kernel), structurally impossible on the `/v1/messages` proxy (the harness runs tools there); witness-keying of the tier-2 key, a cross-process FILL pool, and the speculative-serve `ProvisionalSink` are named **unbuilt**. Law T (sound-before-serve) is the polarity flip from vCache's A2 — a stale tool result *corrupts*, it does not merely *cost*.

- [Long-running agent loops: make fak the loop kernel, not another cron (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/LONG-RUNNING-AGENT-LOOPS-2026-06-25.md) — the operating-system-shaped strategy for rolling cron/launchd/Scheduled Tasks, cloud and remote nodes, phone/Slack/WhatsApp control, notifications, foreground vs background sessions, and green-thread-like logical loops into one fak surface. The key split: schedulers and chat are interrupt sources; fak should own loop identity, admission, leases, run ledgers, task snapshots, witnessed completion, notification discipline, and cache-aware scheduling. First shipped slice: `internal/loopmgr` plus `fak loop append|run|status` provide the hash-chained loop-event ledger, OS-scheduler wrapper, and fold; `tools/issue_resolve_dispatch.py` and `tools/issue_resolve_progress.py` are the first producers; `tools/register_issue_dispatch.ps1` is the first Task Scheduler adapter migrated through `fak loop run`, while Mac dogfood and other scheduler paths remain next.
- [The gardening bundle: default-on the cleanup we run by hand (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/GARDENING-BUNDLE-DEFAULT-ON-2026-06-25.md) — the gardening-workload companion to the loop-kernel note. fak already has three overlapping self-maintenance orchestrators (`scorecard_control_pane` folds 13 scorecards, `fresh_status` folds 4 domains, `fleet_control_pane loop-audit` runs 19 loops) and a built loop runtime (`loopmgr` ledger + governor + `fak loop`), but nothing fires a gardening pass on a cadence and almost nothing auto-fixes. The converge-and-arm plan: one `tools/garden_bundle.py` fold (`make garden`) over the read-only passes, a daily `garden.yml` + a `--mode garden` host tick, the governor as the brake (`FAK_GARDEN=off` / `min_interval_seconds`), then auto-fix behind a `dos commit-audit` witness gate, then a `fak garden` verb. Rungs 0-2 shipped; 3-4 designed.
- [Inbound prompt-MMU: curate WHAT enters the window (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/INBOUND-PROMPT-MMU-2026-06-25.md) — the INGRESS dual of the result-side `ctxmmu`. fak gates the outbound/result half of the context window end-to-end (quarantine results, adjudicate calls, compact old turns) but the inbound composition — tool DEFINITIONS, system, injected skills/memory — forwards byte-identical on the `fak guard -- claude` passthrough. The epic + rungs to curate the ingress, on-by-default both directions with flags only for opinionated overrides, all under the #555 cache-prefix byte-splice + fail-safe-identity discipline. Rung 1 (`internal/promptmmu` `CompactInboundTools`, denied-tool-def pruning) SHIPPED; cache geometry forces it to fire at the session-start/RESET prefix rebuild, refusing pre-breakpoint prunes that would bust the session cache.
- [The system-prompt MMU: fak owns its own base context (2026-06-29)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SYSTEM-PROMPT-MMU-2026-06-29.md) — the AUTHORSHIP dual of the inbound prompt-MMU. #751 prunes a harness-authored prompt as it passes through; this epic takes ownership of the *composition* of the head — a fak-first base context where the irreducible resident spine is fak's own concepts (the attention-sink anchor, byte-identical every turn) and the harness's rules/skill-menu/environment become a queried, paged, append-after-the-breakpoint overlay assembled from the same capability substrate the skill loader (#1103) already ships. The two end-states: (a) the minimal base where the resident head is *only* fak plus a retrieval affordance, and (b) the live base where the prompt is a first-class object fak rewrites at runtime by page-in+mask under a witness gate. The cache doctrine is REGIME-SCOPED, not universal: "append-and-mask, never edit-in-place" is a hard law only where fak does *not* own the cache (the provider passthrough and the proxy-to-local-engine regimes, whose radix-tree-keyed prefix cache goes cold the moment the head changes — Manus' measured ~10×); when fak owns the engine it keeps the pre-RoPE `Kraw` plane and can mutate the head while keeping survivors reusable via **bit-exact span deletion + re-RoPE** (witnessed `max|Δ|=0`, live behind `FAK_INKERNEL_KVMMU`) — though relocated-span *reuse* is not shipped (the repo's own audit faults it to recompute). Grounds the fak-first inversion in attention geometry (regime-independent) plus a cache-stability reason on the passthrough path, states the five load-bearing invariants (spine byte-identical on the provider path; append-and-mask in the provider-uncontrolled regime; safety-critical always resident; pointers-not-bodies with a bounded index; self-modification witness-gated, versioned, append-mostly — the agent never rewrites its spine), maps the built-but-request-path-dead substrate this would *wire* rather than reinvent (`cachemeta.PromptSegment`/`promptmmu`/`ctxplan`/`capindex`/`contextq`/`ctxmmu`/`ctxresidency`/`sessionreset` plus the regime-B `model`/`radixkv`/`kvmmu` span machinery), and lays out six rungs from a new `internal/syspromptmmu` spine to the `fak debug` re-derivation surface that feeds #1217. Planning + tickets only.

- [vCache — a virtual API cache over providers we don't control (2026-06-24)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/VCACHE-VIRTUAL-API-CACHE-2026-06-24.md) — the active control plane proposed *on top of* the passive `internal/cachemeta` tier: treat provider prompt-caching as virtual memory we can observe but not address (vBlock = virtual page, a warm provider prefix = physical frame, the manifest = page table, the request scheduler = MMU), and recall a unit by shaping the *order, shape, and timing* of requests so the provider serves the prefix from its own cache. Audit-grounded: every `cachemeta` symbol checked against HEAD (the fabricated `CacheLane` reference removed; the real seam is `ShapeGLMTurnSegmentWitnessed` + `glm_coherence.go`), the Anthropic per-model min-prefix corrected to 1024 (Opus 4.8 / Sonnet 4.6 / 4.5; 4096 is Haiku 4.5), and the economics (break-even N≥2/≥3, Zipf `s≈1.74` for "7 anchors→85%", chain-horizon `C₀=103`, the 300× recall-by-rebuild loss) independently re-derived. Phased M1–M5 plan + four adversarial laws (warmth is a belief never a boolean; fingerprint the wire bytes; the warm primitive has an irreducible race; calibrate-don't-assume on implicit providers).

Maps DBOS/Temporal durable timers, Durable-Object hibernation+Alarms, CRaC afterRestore, etcd/Chubby fencing tokens, and Letta sleep-time memory onto fak's half-built, DISCONNECTED time primitives (`internal/resume` idle-vs-TTL shipped shadow-only, `session.WaitResume`/`WarmKVSplicer` unwired with `sessionimage.KVIncluded=false` → always cold re-prefill, `leaseref` TTL without a fence = #906-C1, `bgloop` fixed interval). Names the net-new layer — dormancy clock, rehydration orchestrator + rungs (lease-fence/cred/recall/cache), durable wake + duty-cycle, time-travel test harness — as the epic's ten children (#1179-1192). Planning/research only, no code.

- [idea-scout triage: AgenticOS / intent-oriented secure OS (#770) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-agenticos-intent-os-triage-2026-06-26.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.21129 (Zhao et al., "AgenticOS: An Intent-Oriented Secure Operating System Architecture for Autonomous AI Agents"): "resource exposure + permission checks" OS security fails once an agent runtime is compromised, because the attacker composes POSIX primitives past the user's task authorization; AgenticOS reframes the OS from a "resource manager" into an "intent filter" — agents submit structured **intent declarations** → the system synthesizes a least-privilege env with **mandatory mediation, auditing, and information-flow constraints** — via a four-layer kernel (Ghost Kernel, Logic Shutter, Agent Capsule, Semantic Boundary Gateway) + Intent ABI / Manifest-Only Runtime / Weaver capability generation / native-Skill admission. Verdict: **prior art to cite** — the cleanest **OS-altitude** statement of fak's founding premise, and its four required properties map onto shipped fak seams that realize them **in userspace** (default-deny capability floor, the one in-process syscall boundary, the witness/decision journal, result-admit quarantine + `wirescreen` + `SinkGate`). Same side of the trust boundary as fak (not a threat). The four-layer **OS-rebuild** architecture + Weaver synthesis are **not adopted** — fak's bet is one userspace binary at the tool-call seam ([one-binary-one-surface](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/explainers/one-binary-one-surface.md)), not a new kernel; the honest fence is that an OS-altitude filter mediates a strictly larger primitive set at a strictly larger adoption cost.
- [idea-scout triage: Kamera / position-invariant multimodal KV cache (#583) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-kamera-position-invariant-kv-triage-2026-06-26.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.23581 (Ma, Eitzinger, Koestler, Wellein, "Kamera: Unified Position-Invariant Multimodal KV Cache for Training-Free Reuse"): prefix caches serve reuse only at a fixed leading position, so multimodal agents re-encode the same video frames / UI screenshots on every look-back; naive non-prefix KV reuse loses the **cross-chunk conditioning** a chunk absorbs from neighbours, and the loss is **asymmetric** — the direct readout is recovered free by the standard **state-merge**, but a diffuse low-rank residue in deep layers remains, invisible to single-hop retrieval yet **halving multi-hop accuracy**; Kamera repairs it with a training-free **low-rank conditioning patch** + one **RoPE re-rotation** operator across MLA/GQA/MHA (recovers full task accuracy on MM-NIAH + 2-page doc-QA, reconstructs KV within bf16 rounding in a production SGLang kernel across six backbones; strongest in vision/video). Verdict: **prior art to cite** — the paper fak's own [ON-DEMAND-CONTEXT-KV-REUSE](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/ON-DEMAND-CONTEXT-KV-REUSE-2026-06-19.md) note §2.2/§2.3 anticipated and left open (CacheBlend cross-attention loss + MiniPIC position-independent-but-insufficient), now characterized precisely and given a training-free repair — **and a candidate repair** for the conservative RECOMPUTE/REFUSE fault fak's #109 non-prefix-KV audit (`internal/model/nonprefix_kvreuse_audit_test.go`) takes by design. **Adopt only at fak's reserved corrective-path tier (ON-DEMAND §6 Step 5, at #109 × the governed vision seam #399) — NOT in this increment** (a GPU/kernel epic + it needs a gate fak lacks). **One named invariant:** Kamera's bar is full task accuracy + within-bf16-rounding KV, not fak's bit-exact last-logit; because the loss is asymmetric a patched reuse can pass fak's single-last-logit #109 oracle (a single-hop-shaped probe) while halving multi-hop accuracy — so any future patch that promotes a RECOMPUTE fault to a served HIT must clear a **multi-hop** cross-chunk-binding quality probe, never the single-logit check alone. Not a threat (a performance capability on the same side).
- [idea-scout triage: joint intent+harm verification (#910) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-intent-harm-joint-verification-triage-2026-06-26.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26377 (Thota, Lei, Thangaraj, Jonnalagadda, Nilizadeh, "Verifying Intent and Harm: A Unified Defense Against LLM-Generated Threats"): prompt-only and response-only defenses miss attacks that exploit the **separation** between adversarial **intent** (in the prompt) and actionable **harm** (only in the response); the paper proposes a verify-before-deliver framework — a specialized **Intent Analyst** (scores prompt intent) + a specialized **Harm Analyst** (scores response harm) + a **Judge** that resolves conflicts (reported F1 0.90→0.95, ASR 4.1%, benign-sensitive FPR 0.12→0.06 across jailbreaks/prompt-injection/phishing/cyber-abuse/harmful-content, tested under adaptive attackers who know the verifier). Verdict: **prior art to cite** — the join-intent-with-harm thesis is fak's **two-sided adjudication** design at the detector altitude: the kernel already splits the same axis structurally (`k.Decide` folds **only** the pre-call **intent** chain; `k.AdmitResult` is the in-code documented **dual of Decide** and folds the result-side **harm** chain — quarantine + IFC taint + `wirescreen`/`SinkGate` egress floor), and the `dos verify` / `dos commit-audit` referee re-checks claimed intent against the actual diff-borne harm. The three-LLM-analyst + Judge **mechanism is NOT adopted** — it is a learned detector, and fak's recorded position is **detector-is-not-the-floor** ([defensive-misdirection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-defensive-misdirection-triage-2026-06-23.md), [AUC-is-not-detection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-probe-auc-evaluation-protocol-triage-2026-06-23.md)); the paper's own adaptive-attacker result is the evidence that a learned verifier is evadable where fak's default-deny capability floor the model "can't talk past" is not. **Named residual:** the Harm Analyst scores **content harm in text** (the model emitting phishing/harmful words) that fak's capability gate does not score at the tool-call seam — a genuine best-effort-detector rung fak hosts **above** its floor, not on the load-bearing path. Not a threat (a parallel defense on the same side of the boundary).
- [idea-scout triage: ShareLock / multi-tool threshold tool-poisoning against MCP (#911) (2026-06-26)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-sharelock-multitool-threshold-poisoning-triage-2026-06-26.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.27027 (Liu, Han, Liu, Dong, Ruan, "ShareLock: A Stealthy Multi-Tool Threshold Poisoning Attack Against MCP"): a Tool Poisoning Attack that fragments its malicious instruction with **Shamir's (t, n) threshold secret-sharing** across MULTIPLE innocent-looking MCP tool descriptions, reconstructing the hidden instruction only on a **trigger (a server update)** — claiming **information-theoretic** stealth (no description below threshold reveals intent), >90% success, and provable outperformance of single-tool poisoning against **tool-description-based detectors**. Verdict: **prior art to cite + a real threat whose consequence the capability floor already contains** — ShareLock attacks the **detection layer** fak deliberately keeps **off the load-bearing path** (`CLAIMS.md` "Honest ceiling": detection is ~100% evadable, **non-load-bearing**), so its core move (disperse-to-evade a description scanner) is **neutralized by construction** against a floor that never reads the descriptions for a verdict and gates the resulting **action** (default-deny capability lock, units 15/29) and **result** (result-admit quarantine, unit 48) instead. ShareLock is the cleanest external **information-theoretic** proof of fak's *detector-is-not-the-floor* thesis, alongside [defensive-misdirection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-defensive-misdirection-triage-2026-06-23.md) / [AUC-is-not-detection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-probe-auc-evaluation-protocol-triage-2026-06-23.md) / [MCPPrivacyDetector](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mcp-privacy-leakage-triage-2026-06-23.md). **Named residual:** fak does not screen inbound third-party tool descriptions, and a poisoned description can still induce a **policy-ALLOWED** call with malicious arguments — the standing residual of any capability floor, **contained** (not intercepted) by IFC taint + egress sink-gating. The Shamir-sharing mechanism is **not adopted** (adding a description scanner is the anti-pattern ShareLock refutes); the smallest honest follow-on is to treat a downstream **tool-definition change** as a witnessed provenance event (the trigger fires on server update), filed against the `fak_refute_witness` / `fak_changes` seam. No change to `tools/idea_scout.py` — surfaced and scored correctly (topic mcp-security, score 53).
- [idea-scout triage: teaching software engineering with LLM + MCP (#1009) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-llm-mcp-se-education-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.19167 (Chen, Keung, Li, Shao, Li, Ma, "Teaching Software Engineering with LLM and MCP Integration: From Classroom to Industry Practice"): a software-engineering **EDUCATION / pedagogy** study that embeds LLM- and MCP-driven tools into a collaborative **teaching model** (daily teaching, code assistance, engineering simulations) plus industry-internship partnerships, to bridge classroom instruction and industrial workflows. Verdict: **close / not adopted — out of kernel scope** — fak is a runtime trust + performance gate at the tool-call seam, not a curriculum, teaching platform, or learning framework; the paper proposes **no system fak would adopt, no attack to defend against, and no mechanism-level prior art** for fak's adjudication / cross-turn-reuse design (a clean off-mission sibling of the [PrologMCP capability/security miscategorization](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-prologmcp-symbolic-tool-triage-2026-06-24.md)). **Recorded residual (context, not a citation):** the paper is one more external data point that **MCP is moving into mainstream industrial — and now academic — SE practice**, the adoption trend that makes a default-deny capability floor on MCP tool calls worth shipping; it is kept as *why-now* context, never cited as prior art for a fak mechanism. **Scout calibration:** surfaced under `mcp-security` (score 47, the lowest of the day's three hits) on a bare `model context protocol` / `mcp (title)` keyword match + freshness — a true **on-topic-by-keyword, off-mission-by-content** candidate, the scout working **as designed** (judges new-and-on-topic, never worth-building; hands to human triage). No change to `tools/idea_scout.py`.
- [idea-scout triage: where do CoT training gains land in agents? (#1008) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-cot-training-gains-agents-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26935 (Liu, Wang, Jing, Zhou, Liu, "Where Do CoT Training Gains Land in LLM based Agents?"): an **interpretability / training-analysis** study that asks where CoT-training gains land — in **changing the action through generated reasoning** (CoT actions) or in **predicting the action directly from the prompt** with no CoT (prompt actions) — and finds, across checkpoints, that **prompt-action quality improves substantially**, i.e. much of the gain lands in the direct prompt→action mapping rather than in reasoning-driven action change, consistent with prior **CoT-unfaithfulness / post-hoc-rationalization** findings. Verdict: **prior art to cite — not adopted, not a threat** — fak never reads the model's verbalized reasoning for a verdict and never trusts a self-report; it gates the resulting **action** at the tool-call seam (default-deny capability floor) and re-checks claimed work against the **diff** (`dos verify` / `dos commit-audit`), so this is independent **training-time** evidence for fak's **detector-is-not-the-floor / witness-not-self-report** bet (the action is largely fixed by the prompt before the CoT is written, so a CoT-reading detector audits a post-hoc narrative). It is the **CoT-as-explanation** sibling of the contested **attention-as-explanation** demotion in fak's reward-over-spans epic [#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861)/[#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862) ([witnessed-span-attention-validity](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-witnessed-span-attention-validity-2026-06-26.md)): a self-generated explanation is a **proposal to verify against an action-level witness**, never an accepted causal account. **Recorded residual (NOT adopted):** high prompt-action quality means CoT tokens are non-load-bearing on the easy mass of steps — a **token-economy** lever for the `fak dojo` gym ([#951](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/951)) / token-saving-defaults program — but only behind a **per-model, per-task accuracy acceptance gate fak lacks**, and the paper itself shows CoT still **changes the action on the hard tail**, so blind CoT-dropping is unsafe and explicitly not shipped. **Scout calibration:** surfaced under `agent-model-arch` (score 50) on genuine `training (title)` / `checkpoint` / `reasoning` terms + freshness — correctly on-topic and **closer-to-mission** than the day's #1009 pedagogy hit; the scout working **as designed**. No change to `tools/idea_scout.py`.
- [idea-scout triage: MIRROR / novelty-constrained memory-guided MCTS red-teaming for agentic RAG (#1007) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mirror-novelty-mcts-redteam-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26793 (Singh, Murillo, Sekiya, Unno, Suga, "MIRROR: Novelty-Constrained Memory-Guided MCTS Red-Teaming for Agentic RAG"): an **offensive cross-surface attack GENERATOR** for multimodal agentic RAG — memory-guided Monte Carlo tree search that conditions candidate generation on retrieved context under a **deterministic Novelty Gate** (rejects any candidate matching the retrieval set under normalized comparison) across **text poisoning / image injection / direct-query / orchestrator-level tool manipulation**, motivated by measuring **73-84% exact template duplication** in existing surface-specific red-teaming. Verdict (three-part, the shape of [#909](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-out-of-band-injection-defense-taxonomy-triage-2026-06-26.md) / [#911](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-sharelock-multitool-threshold-poisoning-triage-2026-06-26.md)): **(1) prior art to cite** — MIRROR is the **SOTA academic form of fak's own dynamic red-team** (`internal/agentdojo`'s `{plain,obfuscated,paraphrased}` adaptivity axis + `examples/agentdojo-redteam`'s marker-free generative expander) and the **named answer** to the #909 follow-on (make fak's AgentDojo-style ASR battery adaptive, defense-aware, and **cross-surface**, not a static injection set); its deterministic Novelty Gate is the formal sibling of fak's own `tools/idea_scout.py` dedup/novelty rungs (seen-cache + Jaccard near-dup rejection). **(2) A real threat whose CONSEQUENCE the structural floor already contains** — MIRROR's entire edge is **novelty engineered to evade template/pattern detectors**, but fak's full-stack defense taints by **PROVENANCE not content**, so the egress/destructive sink is barred *"regardless of phrasing"* (`internal/agentdojo/agentdojo.go`: ASR(full-stack)==0 vs ASR(detection-only)>0) — the novelty axis is **invariant against the floor by construction**, the same outcome as [ShareLock #911](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-sharelock-multitool-threshold-poisoning-triage-2026-06-26.md); the novelty advantage lands entirely on the detection-only layer fak keeps **off the load-bearing path** (~100% evadable, by design). **Named residual:** containment is not a *measured number* — fak has no adaptive cross-surface ASR-under-containment metric, and the **image-injection** (#290, `internal/model/multimodal`, fail-closed `MultimodalModeQuarantine`) / **orchestrator** (gateway/MCP, adjudicated tool call) surfaces are governed but unmeasured against an adaptive generator. **(3) Mechanism NOT adopted** — fak is a defense; the one-binary zero-dep kernel does not generate attacks (no MCTS / memory / LLM-conditioned generator on the request path; `OUT_OF_DIRECTION` would refuse it). The smallest honest follow-on is the **evaluation upgrade** (expand `internal/agentdojo` toward a novelty-constrained cross-surface generator + add the image/orchestrator surfaces, turning the standing `docs/industry-scorecard/security.md` "no measured adaptive ASR" fence into a tracked agentdojo-lane task), filed not built — with the fence that MIRROR is cited as a **methodology + a contained threat**, never as evidence fak's containment is adaptively robust. No change to `tools/idea_scout.py` — surfaced and scored correctly (topic `prompt-injection-defense`, score 50).
- [idea-scout triage: how reliable is your jailbreak judge? / ASR-judge calibration + adversarial robustness (#1097) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-jailbreak-judge-asr-reliability-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.25487 (Yang Gao, "How Reliable Is Your Jailbreak Judge? Calibration and Adversarial Robustness of Automated ASR Scoring"): a **measurement-validity** study that checks the automated **judge** assigning nearly every reported attack-success-rate (ASR) — a safety classifier or a prompted chat model — against **596 human-labeled** HarmBench completions, then attacks it. The two families fail in opposite ways: the dedicated classifier **over-flags** (P **0.835**, R **0.974**); three LLM-as-judges keep high precision (**0.81-0.94**) but **erratic recall (0.06-0.65)**, so the same responses yield very different ASR by judge. **Benign framing wrappers** that leave the harmful text intact flip **every LLM-judge 57-100%** (a single prepended refusal sentence = **39-88%**); the classifier resists surface attacks (**≤6.7%**) but a small-budget **white-box GCG** on its open weights flips **70%** of its confident true positives (21/30) — an 80-sample audit confirms the flips left the harm intact. Verdict: **prior art to cite — not adopted, not a threat** — it is measured, external evidence for fak's **detector-is-not-the-floor / witness-not-self-report** thesis and a direct validation of fak's **choice of success criterion**: fak's own ASR (`asr_fullstack=0` = 0/38, `asr_detection=0.763` = 29/38, `benign_completion_rate=1`) is assigned by **no judge model at all** — `internal/agentdojo/agentdojo.go` computes `succeeded := injectionReachedContext && sinkExecuted` from deterministic adjudicator verdicts (`VerdictQuarantine` / `VerdictDeny`; the code comment reads *"Deterministic, in-process, no model"*), `catch_reasons` drawn from the closed structural vocabulary (`TRUST_VIOLATION` 29 / `MALFORMED` 9). Because there is no judge model in fak's success decision, the three attack families the paper documents (framing wrappers, prepended-refusal, GCG-on-judge-weights) are **out of fak's metric by construction** — you cannot frame your way past a `VerdictDeny` that gates **PROVENANCE** (tainted→sink), not content (same shape as [MIRROR #1007](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mirror-novelty-mcts-redteam-triage-2026-06-27.md) / [ShareLock #911](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-sharelock-multitool-threshold-poisoning-triage-2026-06-26.md)). The metric-side twin of [AUC-is-not-detection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-probe-auc-evaluation-protocol-triage-2026-06-23.md) / [defensive-misdirection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-defensive-misdirection-triage-2026-06-23.md) and the [FRONTIER survey](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/FRONTIER-AGENT-LEADERBOARD-SURVEY-2026-06.md) HAL *"benchmarks gameable to near-perfect without solving tasks"* anchor. **Honest fence (carried forward):** the immunity is specific to fak's **structural flow-reachability witness** — the day fak reports a **judge-mediated** ASR (a content-harm probe, or any external benchmark whose ASR is LLM-graded and that fak compares against), it must adopt the paper's protocol: report **judge precision/recall on a human-labeled slice**, report **ASR corrected for judge precision**, and include an **adversarial check of the judge**. **Mechanism not adopted** (a measurement-validity result, no kernel surface). No change to `tools/idea_scout.py` — surfaced and scored correctly (topic `prompt-injection-defense`, score 47).
- [idea-scout triage: data-centric survey of privacy in LLM agents (#1098) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-agent-privacy-data-centric-survey-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26627 (Lahjouji, Colaco, "Agents That Know Too Much: A Data-Centric Survey of Privacy in LLM Agents"): a **survey** that organizes LLM-agent privacy around the **data an agent touches** — taxonomizing the data sources (databases, document collections, external APIs, agent memory, cross-session state), the privacy risk each creates (**query leakage, intermediate-result exposure, memory-write vulnerabilities, inter-agent messaging**), and the **governance mechanisms** that address them (it names **information-flow control** + access control), then maps the benchmarks and identifies what is missing. Verdict: **prior art to cite + a real multi-channel threat fak's own IFC governance gates UNEVENLY by provenance** — fak ships one of the two governance families the survey names (`internal/ifc`: a provenance taint `Ledger` (`SourceTaint`) → a `SinkClass` (Egress/Exec/Destructive) → `Policy.Gates` refusing a tainted→gated-sink flow, `DefaultGatedSinks`=EGRESS+DESTRUCTIVE, CaMeL-style `Authorize` escape), so the **final-answer/egress** sink and the **secret-shaped intermediate-result** channel (the [#552 result-admit gate](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mcp-privacy-leakage-triage-2026-06-23.md)) are **gated-by-provenance**; but the survey's **query-issuance** channel is gated-by-capability not by a privacy assessment of the query content, **memory-write** rides the [memory-view contract](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/MEMORY-VIEW-CONTRACT-2026-06-26.md) read-side only, and **inter-agent messages** cross a boundary the session-scoped taint ledger does not provably propagate across — all **gated-by-capability-only or unmeasured** — and fak reports **no measured privacy-leakage number** (the same *containment-is-not-a-measured-number* residual as [MIRROR #1007](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mirror-novelty-mcts-redteam-triage-2026-06-27.md), now stated for the privacy axis). **Mechanism NOT adopted** (a survey, no kernel component); the smallest honest follow-on is a **per-channel privacy-posture audit** (the survey's data-source x risk grid → each channel labeled gated-by-provenance / gated-by-capability-only / unmeasured) + a **candidate privacy-leakage metric**, FILED not built — with the fence the survey is cited as field framing + a coverage map, never as evidence fak's privacy containment is complete or measured. The field-level umbrella over the source-specific [MCPPrivacyDetector triage (#552)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-mcp-privacy-leakage-triage-2026-06-23.md), which instantiates one cell (MCP-server returns). No change to `tools/idea_scout.py` — surfaced and scored correctly (topic `prompt-injection-defense`, score 47).
- [idea-scout triage: PRCR / position-rebinding cache reuse for replay-free visual revisiting (#1099) (2026-06-27)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-position-rebinding-cache-reuse-triage-2026-06-27.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26631 (Wang, Ji, Zuo, Ye, Tu, "Position Rebinding Cache Reuse: Replay-Free Visual Revisiting for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning"): interleaved multimodal reasoning revisits visual evidence during multi-step generation and pays for it with **token replay** (re-forwarding selected visual tokens); the shortcut — reusing the historical visual KV cache directly — has a critical failure mode, **cached visual keys are bound to their ORIGINAL positional context**, so reuse under a later decoding context distorts attention and can trigger **SEVERE AUTOREGRESSIVE DECODING COLLAPSE**; PRCR's fix is **position rebinding** (store raw visual KV with original coords, reassign position-compatible coords to selected entries, rebind keys before injecting into the active decoder cache — preserving textual positional continuity + relative visual structure), reporting replay-level-or-better quality, **+5%** average accuracy, and up to **tens-of-thousands×** less visual-revisiting compute. Verdict: **prior art to cite — the collapse-naming sibling of [Kamera #583](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-kamera-position-invariant-kv-triage-2026-06-26.md)** and the second hit in the non-prefix / position-aware visual-KV-reuse neighbourhood fak's own [ON-DEMAND-CONTEXT-KV-REUSE](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/ON-DEMAND-CONTEXT-KV-REUSE-2026-06-19.md) note §2.2/§2.3 anticipated and its **#109** non-prefix-KV audit (`internal/model/nonprefix_kvreuse_audit_test.go`) proves locally. Where Kamera characterized the loss as a diffuse residue that **halves multi-hop accuracy**, PRCR names the **worst case** (an outright collapsed decode) — the strongest external justification yet for fak's **#109 RECOMPUTE/REFUSE** conservative default (*"a failed exactness budget must produce RECOMPUTE/REFUSE, never HIT"*). The sharp insight: fak's shipped EXACT reuse is **prefix-only**, where cached tokens occupy the **same** leading positions on reuse, so PRCR's failure mode **cannot arise on fak's exact surface by construction** — it appears only at the non-prefix splice the #109 audit refuses; PRCR is independent evidence fak's **prefix-only-exact HIT + non-prefix-faults-to-recompute** structure is the safe one. **Adopt the rebinding operator only at fak's reserved corrective-path tier** (ON-DEMAND §6 Step 5, at #109 × the governed vision seam `internal/model/multimodal.go` #399, fail-closed `MultimodalModeQuarantine`) — **NOT in this increment** (a GPU/kernel epic + it needs a quality gate fak lacks). **One named invariant** (carried from the Kamera triage and tightened): a rebinding patch that promotes a RECOMPUTE fault to a served HIT must clear a **multi-hop** cross-chunk quality probe AND a **no-collapse** check — fak's bit-exact-last-logit-or-fault gate already enforces the no-collapse half for free (a within-rounding rebind keeps faulting), so the binding precondition for USING a rebind is the multi-hop probe fak still lacks. Not a threat (a performance capability on the same side). No change to `tools/idea_scout.py` — surfaced and scored correctly (topic `kv-prefix-cache-reuse`, score 47).
- [idea-scout triage: progress advantage — a free RL-post-training step reward for LLM agents (#1122) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-progress-advantage-rl-posttraining-triage-2026-06-28.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26080 (Oh, Li, Park, Yeh, Mallick, Li, "Neglected Free Lunch from Post-training: Progress Advantage for LLM Agents"): process reward models give step-level LLM evaluation but are prohibitively hard to build for **agentic** settings (long-horizon, irreversible actions, stochastic feedback defeat annotation + Monte-Carlo at scale); the paper shows **RL post-training already contains the step-level signal** — under a general stochastic MDP the **log-prob ratio between the RL-trained policy and its reference policy exactly recovers the optimal advantage** (termed **progress advantage**: annotation-free, domain-agnostic, a free byproduct of the standard post-training pipeline), validated on test-time scaling / uncertainty quantification / failure attribution across 5 benchmarks + 4 model families, beating confidence baselines and **surpassing dedicated trained reward models**. Verdict: **prior art to cite — at the thesis level, with a sharp boundary** — the paper's "the existing pipeline already contains the step-level signal, so train no dedicated judge" is the **reward-modeling-side sibling** of fak's witness referee (`dos verify` / `dos commit-audit` grade a claim against the **diff git actually recorded** — a derived, annotation-free witness — not a trained reward model or the worker's self-report), and the empirical "free signal beats trained PRMs" is independent support for that **don't-build-the-judge** bet. **Sharp fence:** progress advantage is the policy's **own log-probability** (benchmarked against **confidence-based** baselines), a **model-internal self-report**; fak's recorded **detector-is-not-the-floor / witness-not-self-report** stance ([defensive-misdirection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-defensive-misdirection-triage-2026-06-23.md), [AUC-is-not-detection](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-probe-auc-evaluation-protocol-triage-2026-06-23.md)) keeps a signal read off the model's own probabilities **above** the trust floor, never **on** it — the **policy-log-prob sibling** of the CoT-as-explanation demotion in the [#1008 CoT-training triage](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-cot-training-gains-agents-triage-2026-06-27.md) and the attention-as-explanation demotion in [#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861)/[#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862) (a self-generated signal is a **proposal verified against an action-level witness**, never an accepted causal account). **Not adopted as a capability** — fak does not RL-post-train, and the "free lunch" needs paired RL-policy + reference-policy log-probs for the SAME served model that **fak's third-party/local fleet has no reference policy for**, so the signal is **not even computable** on fak's models; no kernel surface (same off-mission shape as #1008 / [#1098 privacy survey](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-agent-privacy-data-centric-survey-triage-2026-06-27.md)). **Not a threat.** **One recorded residual, NOT adopted:** progress advantage as a **cheap proposal signal** for fak's trajectory graders (the paper's **failure-attribution** application maps onto fak's failure-to-witness need — fleet closure-honesty + the `fak dojo` predict→run→measure→eval→calibrate gym [#951](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/951)), gated behind a paired-policy availability fak lacks and fenced as **never-the-floor**. **Scout calibration:** surfaced under `agent-model-arch` (score 44) on genuine `training (title)` + freshness — correctly on-topic; the **third** recent training-time `agent-model-arch` hit fak cannot adopt as a capability (after #1008; cf. #861/#862), an on-topic-by-keyword/off-mission-by-content pattern worth watching but **not** a scoring bug (these still yield citable thesis-level prior art). No change to `tools/idea_scout.py`.
- [idea-scout triage: Tool Suppression under joint tool-call + JSON-schema constraints (#1121) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-tool-suppression-constraint-tax-triage-2026-06-28.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.25605 (Li, Zhang, Lv, "Constraint Tax in Open-Weight LLMs: An Empirical Study of Tool Calling Suppression Under Structured Output Constraints"): a **serving-side** result — when Tool Calling and a JSON-Schema output constraint are enabled **jointly**, multiple **open-weight** model families **stop invoking tools** while keeping **high schema compliance**, a phenomenon it names **Tool Suppression** (a **"Constraint Tax"** the structured-output constraint silently levies on the tool-calling capability), reproduced across model families/settings; each capability is functional **in isolation**. Verdict: **prior art to cite + empirical validation of fak's [#907](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/907) "one canonical internal shape" decision** — fak models tool-CALLING **as** the schema (`grammar.Grammar` → a `oneOf`-of-tools JSON Schema → the `response_format` carrier OR a native logit mask [#929]), so the **two-competing-constraints** configuration that produces Tool Suppression (an independent output `response_format` stacked on a tool-calling turn) is exactly the one fak's unified shape **avoids**; the paper strengthens #907/#929 rather than asking fak to build anything. **A self-inflicted failure mode fak can induce two ways:** the native guided-decode mask (`internal/model/constraint.go`, behind `FAK_NATIVE_GUIDED_DECODE=1`, which **defaults OFF** — a schema mask is never stacked on a tool-calling turn unless an operator opts in, an accidental protection), and the [#907 passthrough](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-structured-output-decoding-2026-06-26.md) (`internal/gateway/http.go:464`) forwarding a client `response_format` to an upstream vLLM/SGLang alongside tools, where any suppression is the **upstream's** behavior — **OBSERVED/relayed, not a fak action** (the controlled-vs-observed conflation boundary). **The load-bearing trust-floor point (why it is labelled `trust-floor`):** a suppressed tool call is **invisible** to fak's default-deny adjudication floor — `internal/adjudicator/decide.go` `Adjudicate(ctx, *abi.ToolCall)` only ever receives a call that **was** emitted, so Tool Suppression is a capability **false-negative below the floor** (no call = nothing to deny = trivially "safe" to a deny-bad-calls gate) that an adjudicator **structurally cannot** catch by adjudicating calls; detection requires **observing the absence** (tool offered + joint schema active + zero calls + schema-valid prose), an **observability** ask fak does not measure today. **Not adopted** as a new mechanism (the right design ships as #907); **not** a classic threat (a constraint-interaction defect, no adversary). **One residual, FILED not built:** a gateway "tool-suppression-suspected" observability counter, gated behind a **served-open-weight reproduction this win32 dev box cannot run** (the "expected a tool call" half needs calibration — shipping it now would be an unwitnessed "expected" claim). No capability code change; no change to `tools/idea_scout.py` (surfaced + scored correctly under topic `tool-call-adjudication`, score 44, on-topic and close-to-mission).
- [idea-scout triage: EpiKV — KV eviction by the epiphany score, no attention matrix (#1123) (2026-06-28)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/RESEARCH-epikv-attention-free-eviction-triage-2026-06-28.md) — triage of arXiv:2606.26472 (Kolawole, Smith, "Epiphany-Aware KV Cache Eviction Without the Attention Matrix" / EpiKV): a **serving-side** eviction **policy** — existing methods rank tokens by **attention weight**, which the paper argues is a noisy importance proxy in long reasoning traces AND **prohibits fused kernels** by forcing the model to materialize the attention matrix; EpiKV instead scores tokens by the **epiphany score** (the change in the model's internal representation, read from the forward pass with no attention matrix), training-free and custom-kernel-free. Verdict: **prior art to cite + validation of fak's attention-as-explanation demotion ([#861](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/861)/[#862](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/862)) in the EVICTION-POLICY domain + a candidate fused-kernel-friendly importance POLICY for fak's policy-agnostic exact-eviction MECHANISM**. fak's value-add is the bit-exact mid-run evictor (`internal/model/kvcache.go` `Evict`, the paged twin `internal/model/paged_evict.go` `PagedKV.Evict` [#33], the `internal/kvmmu/` governance evictor) — it evicts a span handed to it and leaves the cache byte-for-byte `== never-saw-it` (`max|Δ|=0`), so the importance scorer is a **swappable input**; fak already shipped ONE policy — [#856](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/856) "attention-informed exact eviction — evict coldest-by-attention via the existing bit-exact evictor" (CLOSED, kvmmu lane), fed by the post-softmax attention mass `internal/model/attn_observer.go` emits. **The load-bearing fak-specific point:** #856's attention mass is materialized for free on fak's CPU softmax seam, but a **fused GPU attention kernel** (FlashAttention/FlashInfer — fak's production decode direction) does NOT materialize the attention matrix, so carrying coldest-by-attention onto the fused path forces materializing it — the exact tax EpiKV names — whereas the epiphany score (a hidden-state delta) is forward-pass-readable without it; EpiKV is the fused-kernel-compatible importance signal for the gap #856 leaves on fak's fused path. **NOT adopted as a mechanism:** fak has an attention-mass observer but NO hidden-state-delta observer (the epiphany score's carrier), and proving any lossy eviction policy preserves answer quality on long reasoning traces needs a **served long-CoT eviction-quality benchmark this win32 dev box cannot run** (host-gated, [AVOID-TESTING-ON-THIS-MACHINE](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/AVOID-TESTING-ON-THIS-MACHINE-2026-06-25.md)). **Not a threat** (a performance capability, no adversary). **One residual, FILED not built:** a forward-pass hidden-state-delta observer feeding the kvmmu exact evictor (the representation-delta twin of `attn_observer`→#856), gated on that served witness. The one concrete artifact: a §B2 catalog row in [`docs/awesome-token-efficiency.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/awesome-token-efficiency.md). No capability code change; no change to `tools/idea_scout.py` (surfaced + scored correctly under topic `kv-prefix-cache-reuse`, score 44, on-topic and close-to-mission).

- [The account switcher's single-source problem, and why gem8 "disappeared" (2026-06-25)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/ACCOUNT-SWITCHER-SINGLE-SOURCE-2026-06-25.md) — diagnosis + consolidation path: `claude-accounts observe` (the `job` repo) reads a different roster than `dos accounts` and `fak accounts`, so gem8 reads "tombstoned" in one and "active" in another; and a config dir has TWO credentials (interactive login vs setup `.oauth-token`) that can name different accounts, so one rate-limit bucket shows as several "serving" seats. - [The shared-trunk compile-integrity gap: lease disjointness is not build isolation (2026-07-06)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/SHARED-TRUNK-COMPILE-INTEGRITY-GAP-2026-07-06.md) — a witnessed incident (a peer's uncommitted call to an undefined `runSuperloopDrive` broke every session's `cmd/fak` build) exposes a fourth axis the git-admin epic's three named gaps (#822/#834) do not cover. Disjoint file leases (`dos arbitrate`) guarantee ownership disjointness at *file* granularity; Go compiles at *package* granularity, so two agents with disjoint leases in one package still share one build graph — and on a shared dirty tree an agent cannot witness its own change, the one place the witness-not-self-report floor cannot stand. Shows neither `pre-commit` (7 content gates) nor `pre-push` (`dos review` + tier drift) compiles anything, so the runbook's archive-HEAD build stays manual. Proposes raising *atomic commit* from "coherent file set" to "coherent file set proven to compile against HEAD in isolation": a static self-containment rung at the commit seam (`COMMIT_NOT_SELF_CONTAINED`, no build) and an affected-scoped isolated build rung at the push seam (`TRUNK_WOULD_NOT_COMPILE`), both fail-closed with the standard block|warn|off ladder, reusing `affectedtests.Select` and the archive-HEAD technique. Design only; the hook change is park-by-default/sensitive and wants its own issue + warn-soak.
