- [Dispatch-worker context-budget trap: the derived-budget fix and its measured-baseline residual (2026-07-08)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/dispatch-worker-context-budget-trap-2026-07-08.md) — the tracking note commit `8a0fcffbb` referenced but never created. Records the #2972 crash-loop where the claude dispatch worker's guard `--context-budget-tokens` (a flat 48000) sat below the workers' ~62K irreducible turn-1 baseline prompt, so every worker was born over-budget and drained `BUDGET_CONTEXT_EXHAUSTED` on turn 1 (`DebitUsage` debits the FULL resident window each turn) → restarts burned → `CHILD_CRASH`, fleet ship rate 2–9%. Documents the shipped derived-budget fix (`min(claudeGuardBaselineTokens*2, HardContextCap−OutputReserve)` = `min(62000*2, 200000−32000)` = 124000, golden-pinned on the Go + Python sides) and the #3522 follow-up that turned the frozen 62000 baseline into a **floored, raising-only measurement**: `baseline = max(Σ (bytes+3)/4 over the launch constituents readable at launch — AGENTS/llms/CLAUDE/MEMORY + the `route` blob when named via `DISPATCH_STARTUP_BUNDLE`, 62000)`. Because it floors AT the old constant and only ever raises, it closes the organic-orientation-growth hole without the false-confidence trap of a static repo-file sum that *asserts* the fraction bounds the whole (the rejected non-fix) — the floor stays authoritative for every dynamic term the sum can't see. Emits `guard_baseline_tokens`/`guard_context_budget_tokens` as an observable. Residual still open: the per-issue body + Claude Code system prompt (and the `route` blob absent the env, and the injected fleet memory which really lives in the per-project claude memory dir, not a workspace-root MEMORY.md file) are floor-covered only, so runtime attribution — a turn-1 drain emitting a distinct `real_baseline>budget` reason instead of a generic crash — is the highest-preference of the remaining checkable steps.
- [Worktree land merge-reconciliation contract: a rejected apply is a structured refusal, never a silent drop (2026-07-10)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/WORKTREE-LAND-MERGE-RECONCILIATION-2026-07-10.md) — the #1334 land seam's all-or-nothing `git apply` rejects whenever the trunk moved inside the worker's diff region since its pinned base, and the old contract failed open with generic prose — silently dropping the worker's entire already-verified delta, the one outcome the witness-not-self-report floor can never audit. Compares three reconcile algorithms (rebase-before-every-land, `git apply --3way`, serialized-apply-under-lane-lease-with-auto-rebase-on-reject) and picks the third: the fast path stays a plain apply, and conflicts only ever materialize inside the worker's isolated worktree — never as conflict markers on the shared trunk (`--3way`'s disqualifying failure mode). Names the landing session as the deterministic conflict owner (auto-rebase in place; STOP-and-replan on a genuine overlapping-region conflict — never a human merge queue, never a silent drop) and ships the contract half: `land_worktree_diff`'s reject arm now returns a structured refusal (`reason=COLLISION_RISK` from the closed refusal vocabulary — `dos check-reason`: refusal, route-to-replan — plus the git evidence and a replan `next_action`), doctest-pinned, with the STOP invariants (nothing applied, nothing committed, trunk clean, worktree kept as evidence). Composes with the compile-integrity rungs: a clean apply proves *textual* disjointness, not *semantic* compatibility, so the rebase arm re-runs the compile witness in the re-pinned worktree and the push-seam `TRUNK_WOULD_NOT_COMPILE` rung backstops the clean-apply-onto-a-moved-trunk case.
- [tair-kvcache borrow study: one cache-budget-sweep gap filed, the rest present-on-witness (2026-07-10)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/tair-kvcache-borrow-study-2026-07-10.md) — a deep-read of [`alibaba/tair-kvcache`](https://github.com/alibaba/tair-kvcache) @ `6896aae1` (Apache-2.0) scanned for cache/latency techniques fak lacks, borrow-not-vendor, with every candidate **witnessed against the actual tree** before filing. Net result: one genuine high-leverage borrow filed — [#3952](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3952), a single-pass cache-budget→reuse miss-ratio-curve sweep (replay a prefix-access trace over N budgets **plus one unbounded pass** → reuse-vs-budget curve + infinite-cache **theoretical ceiling** + the smallest budget at 99% of it, the ROI **knee**) to size `--compact-history-budget` and the radixkv LRU budget from evidence instead of intuition, reusing `radixkv` as the replay engine and `cacheobs`/`cachevalueledger` as the realized-reuse feeders (upstream `optimizer/analysis/script/run/tradeoff.py` + `manager/optimizer_runner.cc`). The other candidates were **dropped on witness** as already present, the redundancy the witness step exists to catch: the calibration + MAPE-vs-measured gate is present ×3 (`gateway/calibration_corpus_drift_test.go` fails CI on const-vs-corpus drift; `resume_projection.go` exposes OBSERVED−PROJECTED residual gauges + a refit signal; `vcachecal` reports false-warm/false-cold rather than assuming zero) — its only absent remainder is an XGBoost residual model fak's deterministic-auditable ethos would reject; gen-fenced stale-lease reclaim is `leaseref/fence.go` (monotonic fencing token, CAS, halt-and-reacquire on `STALE_LEASE`); single-flight is subsumed by `callavoid`'s break-even + amplification economics; LeafAwareLRU/tiered-demote/quota map to `radixkv`/`cachemeta`/headroom. Fixed-vs-sliding-window TTL deferred (low-leverage; `cachemeta` already separates `AdmittedAt` from `LastAccess`).
- [KernelWiki borrow study: 5 sub-epics + 28 leaves onto existing seams, 47 candidates witnessed (2026-07-10)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/2026-07-10-kernelwiki-study.md) — a deep `/study-repo` pass over [`mit-han-lab/KernelWiki`](https://github.com/mit-han-lab/KernelWiki) @ `76d27b56` (a curated GPU-kernel knowledge base + CI-invariant ingestion pipeline; tooling MIT-style, all borrows **inspire**, no bytes vendored), scanned for the corpus-hygiene disciplines fak's knowledge/claim/ingest surfaces lack. 47 grounded candidates, one capability-witness each **dogfooding fak's own self-index**: **43 PARTIAL, 3 ABSENT, 1 PRESENT**. The signal is not "fak lacks a feature" but "fak has the seam — `freshness.go` DriftKinds, `CLAIMS.md`/`honesty.go:30` one-tag lint, `idea_scout` firehose, `benchauthority` — without the invariant (closed vocab, bidirectional registry, reproducibility floor, committed decision ledger, byte-checkable provenance)." The fileable candidates organize onto **five existing fak seams**, filed as **five single-axis sub-epics** under umbrella epic [#3946](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3946), each **fully decomposed into independently-shippable child leaves** (28 leaves, #4072–#4099): committed decision-ledger + skip-audit closure over `idea_scout.py:445` ([#3947](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3947), 5 leaves); frontmatter-derived regenerated indices + internal citation-graph gate over `internal/devindex/freshness.go` ([#3948](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3948), 7 leaves); evidence-tiered VERIFIED gate + machine-witnessed reproducibility floor over `honesty.go`/`benchauthority` ([#3949](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3949), 6 leaves); version-sensitive-claim registry + cutoff SoT + offline tool-version time-decay ([#3950](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3950), 6 leaves); immutable source-page layer + typed provenance taxonomy + drift re-check generalizing `swebenchsota.go:79` ([#3951](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3951), 4 leaves). Two candidates **deduped into already-open issues** (alias-aware retrieval → [#3925](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3925); object-reuse eval-cache rung → [#3923](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/3923)); **8 Blackwell decode-kernel borrows captured as a file-after-measurement shortlist** (3 ABSENT) rather than filed speculatively; 1 dropped PRESENT. Full 47-candidate ledger with per-candidate verdict + KernelWiki source anchor + fak seam + leaf number, plus the completeness critic's unopened-area disclosure, inside.
- [Decode occupancy/traffic witness landed + A100 ncu measurement gate (2026-07-11)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/2026-07-11-decode-occupancy-witness-measurement.md) — the follow-on that discharges the [KernelWiki study](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/2026-07-10-kernelwiki-study.md)'s **file-after-measurement** gate on its Blackwell decode-kernel shortlist (Cluster G, 8). Lands `internal/compute/decode_occupancy.go` (7 tests green, on origin/main) + its A100 Nsight-Compute harness `tools/dgx_decode_occupancy_ncu.sh`. The file/no-file verdict is **exact** (grid-block counts vs SM counts, operand bytes): flash decode launches one block per query head, so SmolLM2's `nH=9` grid leaves **99 of 108 A100 SMs idle every step** — register-independent — and decode attention is memory-bound at ~0.5 FLOP/byte. Verdict: **4 FILE** (persistent-kernel tail, `__ldcs` L1 hints, CLC tile-scheduling wave-quant tail, MoE launch-fusion), **1 no-gap** (tmem-accumulator-migration — grid-bound not per-SM-bound, the speculative ticket the gate stops), **3 defer** (nvfp4/PDL/CLC-try-cancel are sm_90+/sm_100-only, not A100-measurable). The device ncu corroboration (achieved-occupancy / DRAM-%) was dispatched but the Slack control-bridge readback was transport-wedged this session (`context deadline exceeded`; **no device numbers fabricated**); the note carries the one-command recipe to obtain it when the bridge is healthy.
- [DeepWiki concept study: a fak-native witness-verified repo wiki track — 1 epic + 7 leaves (2026-07-11)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-DEEPWIKI-2026-07-11.md) — a `/study-repo` pass over [`AsyncFuncAI/deepwiki-open`](https://github.com/AsyncFuncAI/deepwiki-open) @ `16f35a0` (MIT, borrows **inspire**, the open reimplementation of Cognition's hosted DeepWiki) + a SOTA scan of **CodeWiki** (arXiv:2510.24428, `CodeWikiBench`) and `open-deepwiki`, scoping the human/LLM-facing **navigable narrative wiki** fak lacks. Reads DeepWiki's two generation prompts (`src/app/[owner]/[repo]/page.tsx`): phase-1 emits a `<wiki_structure>` XML tree (8–12 pages over a fixed taxonomy, `:746-795,829`), phase-2 writes each page grounded **only** in its `relevant_files` with a forced ≥5-file `<details>` header and `Sources:[file:line]()` per claim (`:420-526`), retrieval by FAISS (`api/rag.py:41`). The decisive framing: every tool in the field shares **two weaknesses that are exactly fak's thesis** — (1) citations are LLM-produced and **never resolved against the tree** (`:497-502`; "reduce but do not eliminate hallucination"), and (2) **snapshot staleness** (regenerated on a schedule, "may lag main by hours to days"); meanwhile fak already holds as **ground truth** the structure DeepWiki re-infers with an LLM+FAISS pass (`internal/devindex`). So the fak wiki **seeds structure from the self-index and witnesses every citation** — the two things the field structurally cannot do. Filed as epic [#4277](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/issues/4277) + 7 independently-shippable leaves (#4278–#4284): L1 `fak wiki structure` (deterministic tree from `devindex`, P1 foundation), L2 source-grounded page-gen, L3 witnessed `Sources:[path:line]` resolver (P1 anti-hallucination core), L4 freshness-gated pages (`DriftStaleWikiPage` over `freshness.go`), L5 Mermaid diagrams from the real `refs.go`/`blastradius` graph, L6 claims-aware stub/simulated banner from `CLAIMS.md`, L7 `fak wiki score` coverage/citation-resolve gate. Builds on the queryable-self-index epic [#1287]; **ablated against the sibling KernelWiki index-integrity track** [#3948] so L3/L4 cross-link (#4079/#4077) rather than dupe — that track hardens the *internal fact-index*, this one generates the *narrative wiki*. Nothing built; every borrow is `path:line@16f35a0`-anchored and witnessed PARTIAL/ABSENT before filing.
- [In-flight repair of a sanctioned compiled sidestep: auto-substitute `git push` → `fak sync push` (2026-07-15)](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/notes/IN-FLIGHT-REPAIR-SANCTIONED-SIDESTEP-2026-07-15.md) — answers "if `fak sync push` is such an obvious sanctioned equivalent, why doesn't the guard repair the refused `git push` in flight?" The rewrite-and-execute mechanism already exists — the `VerdictTransform{NewArgs}` verdict applied at `internal/gateway/adjudicate_proposed.go:446-454` — but is scoped to same-tool **argument** edits (secret redaction, `attenuateCLIGrammar`, `_fak_confirm` strip); the `git push → fak sync push` sidestep is only ever surfaced as advisory prose (`reversibilityFamily.hint` → `Detail["remedy"]` → `remedyNote`), and `#4428` "error affordance rewrites" rewrites note **text**, not calls. Designs a conservative, **opt-in** (`FAK_GUARD_AUTOREPAIR=sidestep`) auto-substitution: fire only when the family carries a `fak ` compiled sidestep (`compiledSidestepRemedy`), the call is a **Bash** command (a pure `NewArgs` rewrite — no ABI `NewTool` needed, unlike the MCP-tool variant), and the command is in the **safe-equivalent subset** (bare `git push` with none of `--force`/`--delete`/`--tags`/`--all`/`--mirror`/`--prune`/explicit refspec — structurally decidable via the existing `gitDryRunPreview` flag parser). Sound because `SafePush` pushes the **current branch** non-force ff-only, so bare `git push` ≈ `fak sync push`; the pause is theater for the safe subset and load-bearing only for the dangerous variants (which stay a `RequireWitness` pause — auto-laundering `--force` into a non-force verb would silently change intent). Implementation is **core-locked** (`internal/adjudicator`, `corelockaudit.go:64`) → needs `fak commit --core-lock-maintenance-witness`; the gateway/env wiring is not. Suggests 4 increments (promote `familyRemedyCommands` out of `_test` → substitute verdict in the rung → gateway/env wiring → extend to issue-create/slack/messaging families). Design only; nothing built.

# `CONTRIBUTING.md`

> Source: `CONTRIBUTING.md`

# Contributing to fak / fleet

Thanks for contributing. **Autonomous coding agents are first-class contributors here**
— the same rules below bind a human, a Claude Code session, and a Codex/Cursor/Aider
run alike, because they're enforced *below* the agent layer by git hooks and the DOS
trust kernel, not by trust. This file is the durable contract for everyone — human and
agent alike.

New here and want a small first PR? The [good first popularization tasks](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/docs/adoption/good-first-tasks.md)
board lists doc-sized wins, each naming the exact file to edit and how hard it is.

This file is short on purpose; the deep public guides are `fak/ARCHITECTURE.md` (the
extension model and the layered-DAG tier gates, enforced by `internal/architest`) and
**`fak/EXTENDING.md`** — the golden path if you're a researcher or team who wants to
build an *optimization for a subsystem* (a faster kernel, a new cache backend, a smarter
admission rung) on fak without forking the core.

## Licensing — read this before your first PR

The fak kernel is **Apache-2.0** (`LICENSE`); the project keeps layered-licensing
optionality open while Netra is the steward (see `CLA.md`). Every contribution is gated by
two things — one binding today, one staged:

1. **DCO sign-off on every commit** *(binding today, enforced by a git hook)* — the
   Developer Certificate of Origin (<https://developercertificate.org/>). It certifies you
   wrote the change (or have the right to submit it). Add it with:

   ```
   git commit -s -m "your message"
   ```

   which appends a `Signed-off-by: Your Name <you@example.com>` trailer. The name/email
   must match your commits.

2. **CLA acceptance** *(staged; the text is a **draft pending Netra's legal review and not
   yet binding**)* — see `CLA.md`. The CLA grants Netra the copyright/patent license
   (including the sublicense right) that keeps the project's layered-licensing optionality
   open while Netra is the steward. The sign-off ritual is staged now so the infrastructure
   is ready before the first external PR, but the exact instrument may change on counsel's
   review before it is declared final. Until an automated CLA-assistant is wired up, state
   in your first PR: *"I have read the CLA Document and I hereby sign the CLA"* —
   acknowledging that the text is a draft subject to revision. Corporate contributors
   (employer owns the IP) need a Corporate CLA — contact Netra.

> **Why both, and why now:** the DCO is cheap provenance; the CLA is the relicense-enabling
> grant. Landing them *before the first external PR* is the one irreversible, time-sensitive
> licensing move. **The `CLA.md` text is a draft pending Netra's legal review**; the
> infrastructure is in place, the exact instrument is counsel's call.

Contributions are accepted **inbound = outbound**: your change is licensed to the public
under the same license that governs that part of the tree (today, Apache-2.0 for the
kernel), in addition to the CLA grant to Netra.

## Development workflow

- **Check you're set up first** — `python tools/extend_preflight.py` verifies the git
  guards, the stay-on-trunk state, the ship-stamp convention, and the extension gate
  entry points in one read-only command, then prints the golden path. Building an
  optimization for a subsystem? Start with [`fak/EXTENDING.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/EXTENDING.md).
- **Touching docs? Keep the scorecard honest.** `python tools/docs_scorecard.py --scope
  reachable` grades every reader-reachable doc on five KPIs (freshness, link integrity,
  structure, readability, evidence) and counts *doc-debt* — the concrete defects a cold
  reader can hit (dead links, stale install pins, unresolved placeholders, missing titles,
  strawman-led headlines, orphans). It is read-only; a non-zero exit is a work-list, not a
  block. Regenerate the scorecard snapshot with `--markdown` after a docs pass. This is the whole-corpus analogue of
  `tools/readme_freshness_audit.py`, which checks the front page.
- **Touching the docs site or the FAQ? Keep discoverability honest.** `python
  tools/seo_aeo_scorecard.py --scope core` grades the published Pages surfaces on six
  SEO/AEO KPIs (title, description, headings, links, links_crawlable, answerability)
  plus site-level checks (sitemap, canonical, JSON-LD, `llms-full.txt`, citation_links)
  and counts *seo-debt*. Beyond the presence checks (is the meta/link/JSON-LD there?)
  it runs SUCCESS checks (does it WORK for the consumer): `links_crawlable` flags a link
  that resolves on disk but 404s on the live site, the corpus-wide meta-distinctness pass
  flags a duplicate `<title>`/description search can't tell apart, `citation_links`
  flags a dead llms.txt-map or self-repo GitHub link an answer engine would follow, and
  `llms_full_navigable` flags inlined local links that lost their source-page base path.
  If you
  changed the FAQ or `_config.yml`, re-run `python tools/gen_structured_data.py` to
  regenerate the JSON-LD (CI hard-gates that it is in sync). The discoverability
  **scores** are strategic and live in the private repo (`--transfer`); the tool and the
  read-only work-list are public.
- **Tests run through WSL, not native Windows** — `.\fak\test.ps1` (whole suite) or
  `.\fak\test.ps1 ./internal/<pkg>/`. `go build` / `go vet` work natively; only test
  *execution* is blocked on the Windows host. See the Windows note in
  [`fak/GETTING-STARTED.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/GETTING-STARTED.md) for why. **Never commit a red tree.**
- **Add a feature as a leaf, not a core edit** — `fak new-leaf <name> --tier
  <tier> [--register]` stamps a conforming skeleton and wires the layering/registration.
  The frozen ABI (`internal/abi`) is additive-only and human-owned; everything else
  attaches through a `Register*` seam. `internal/architest` fails the build on an upward/
  cross-tier import, and `CLAIMS.md` requires every claim to carry exactly one of
  `[SHIPPED]`/`[SIMULATED]`/`[STUB]`.
- **Work directly on `main` — do not open a feature branch.** This is the
  single-source-of-truth operator law (`main-is-single-source`): every contributor,
  human or agent, commits to `main` in the main worktree. Creating a side branch or a
  new worktree to route around a dirty/diverged tree is the `OFF_TRUNK` anti-pattern that
  the trunk guard (`tools/githooks/reference-transaction`) and `dos.toml` actively
  **refuse** — so a doc that tells you to "branch first" would send you straight into a
  blocked commit. `git commit -- <paths>` and `git merge` / `git pull --no-rebase` never
  need a clean tree, so a dirty tree is never a reason to branch: pull/merge in place,
  wait for it to settle, or STOP and surface the blocker. Install the guards once per
  clone with `python tools/install_trunk_guard.py` (arms the trunk guard + the
  public-leak scan). The *one* sanctioned worktree is the detached per-worker
  build-isolation tree (#1334 / epic #3165): pinned at trunk HEAD, it lands on `main` via
  the serialized `land_worktree_diff` under the worker's lane lease through `fak worktree
  worker prepare|land|reap|list`, so it is not a branch and never trips `OFF_TRUNK`. That
  is the only worktree exception; feature branches and off-trunk commits remain refused.
- **Commit small and by explicit path**. Prefer the repo verbs: `fak sweep [--json]`
  indexes a dirty shared tree by lane, `fak sweep --apply --lane <lane> -m "<subject>"`
  lands a whole lane group, and `fak commit --path <p> -m "<subject>"` lands a narrower
  slice through the same guarded path. Raw `git commit -- <paths>` is the fallback when the
  binary is unavailable; `git add -A` is never allowed. This is a shared multi-session tree
  — never stage a peer's uncommitted files. **Default: once the tree is green, commit AND
  push — you don't wait to be asked.** Green is `make ci` (build + vet + test +
  claims-lint; tests run under WSL via `./test.ps1` on Windows), after which the
  commit-message / file-admission / public-leak / trunk guards run as git hooks. Pull
  before you start and again before each push; push promptly after each green commit, on the
  trunk, with `git commit -s` (DCO) — never force-push. If a guard refuses (`OFF_TRUNK`), a
  peer merge is in flight, or a blocker stands, reconcile in place or STOP first.
- **Stamp every commit so it can be verified.** Fleet writes Conventional-Commits
  subjects (`feat(scope): …`, `fix(scope): …`, `docs(scope): …`) with a `(fak <leaf>)`
  trailer naming the lane the work lands in — e.g. `fix(gateway): treat same-tick ready
  as positive timeToReady (fak gateway)`. The DOS verify-referee binds "done" to that
  trailer (`dos verify fak <leaf>`); an un-stamped subject is deliberately *not* treated
  as a ship. Use a `docs(scope): …` subject for doc-only changes (a `fix(`/`feat(` prefix
  on a docs-only diff is read as an unwitnessed code claim). The lane names are the
  `[lanes]` in `dos.toml`. This is **in addition to** the DCO sign-off above, which is the
  separate legal-provenance trailer.

## Good first issues — where to start

New here? Browse the [`good first issue`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/labels/good%20first%20issue)
label for scoped, well-defined starter work. If nothing's open, these are the standing
on-ramps — each is additive, ships green through `make ci`, and touches no enforced
guard:

- **Add a per-agent integration recipe** under [`docs/integrations/`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/tree/main/docs/integrations)
  for a harness that doesn't have one yet (the pattern is in the existing
  `claude.md` / `cursor.md` recipes). The lowest-friction first PR.
- **Stamp a new leaf** with `fak new-leaf <name> --tier <tier> [--register]`
  and fill it in — the additive extension path that never edits core. Start from
  [`EXTENDING.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/EXTENDING.md).
- **Retire one doc-debt item** the docs scorecard names —
  `python tools/docs_scorecard.py --scope reachable` prints a work-list of concrete,
  cold-reader defects (a dead link, a stale install pin, a missing title). Fix one,
  regenerate with `--markdown`.
- **Add a real test** for a package the code-quality scorecard flags untested —
  `python tools/code_quality_scorecard.py` names them; a genuine test (never a stub)
  is exactly the contribution that pays back.

Pick one, read the entry doc it points to, and ship it small and by explicit path.

## Reporting issues

Use the GitHub tracker. Security-sensitive reports (a way past the capability floor or the
containment gate) should be raised **privately** — see [`SECURITY.md`](https://github.com/anthony-chaudhary/fak/blob/main/SECURITY.md) — rather
than filed as a public issue.
